readingQuestions.question: 谁没有猫？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does not have a cat?

quizzes.title: The regular calendar
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Weekdays are numbered (星期一 = weekday-one = Monday), months are numbered (二月 = two-month = February). Two patterns replace fourteen English words.

helpMemoryTips.title: Count your week
helpMemoryTips.text: 星期一 Monday … 星期六 Saturday — then Sunday breaks the pattern: 星期天 (or 星期日), the "sky/sun day".

helpMemoryTips.title: Dates run big → small
helpMemoryTips.text: Year 年 → month 月 → day 号 → weekday: 2026年7月2号星期四. Chinese time always zooms from large to small.

quizzes.title: Telling the time: 点 / 分 / 半

sentences.sentence: What time is it now? → 现在____？
It's half past eight. → 八点____。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Clock time is number + 点 (o'clock): 三点 = 3:00. Add 半 for half past and 分 for minutes. 几点? asks the time.

helpMemoryTips.title: 点 = o'clock, 半 = half past
helpMemoryTips.text: 八点 8:00, 八点半 8:30, 八点十分 8:10. Note "two o'clock" is 两点 (liǎng diǎn), never 二点.

quizzes.title: Time goes BEFORE the verb

subjects.display: I sleep at eleven at night.

sentences.sentence: I get up at seven. → 我____起床。
He goes to Beijing tomorrow. → 他____去北京。
We eat at twelve. → 我们____吃饭。
She works on Monday. → 她____上班。
Are you coming this evening? → 你____来吗？
I sleep at eleven at night. → 我晚上____睡觉。
sentences.english: I sleep at eleven at night.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The word-order cliff: English says "I get up at seven"; Chinese sets the scene first — 我七点起床 (I at-seven get up). Time never trails the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Set the scene, then act (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: Subject + WHEN + (WHERE) + verb: 我明天去北京. Putting time at the end (我去北京明天 ✗) is the #1 English-speaker word-order error.

helpMemoryTips.title: Time can also lead
helpMemoryTips.text: For emphasis the time may open the sentence: 明天我去北京. Before the subject or after it — but never after the verb.

quizzes.title: Speaking: my day

subjects.english: Wǒ měitiān qī diǎn qǐchuáng. — I get up at seven every day.
Wǒ zǎoshang hē kāfēi. — I drink coffee in the morning.
Wǒ bā diǎn bàn qù xuéxiào. — I go to school at 8:30.
Wǒmen shí'èr diǎn chī wǔfàn. — We eat lunch at twelve.
Wǎnshang wǒ kàn diànshì. — In the evening I watch TV.
Wǒ shíyī diǎn shuìjiào. — I go to bed at eleven.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Say your daily routine aloud — feel how the time expression always lands before the action.

helpMemoryTips.title: Chunk it: WHEN + DO
helpMemoryTips.text: Pause mentally after the time chunk: 我七点 // 起床. Building the habit aloud installs the word order for free (Z13).

quizzes.title: 在 + place: scene before action

subjects.display: I eat at home. (at home + eat)
We drink tea at the café.

sentences.sentence: I am at home. → 我____家。
I eat at home. (at home + eat) → 我____吃饭。
sentences.english: I eat at home. (at home + eat)

sentences.sentence: He works in Beijing. → 他____工作。
She studies Chinese at school. → 她____学习中文。
We drink tea at the café. → 我们____喝茶。
sentences.english: We drink tea at the café.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 在 zài marks where: 我在家 I'm at home. Doing something somewhere puts the 在-phrase BEFORE the verb: 我在家吃饭 — at home (I) eat.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 在 + place + verb (Z13/Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我在咖啡馆学习 — "I at the café study." English appends "at the café"; Chinese sets the scene before the action. 我学习在咖啡馆 ✗.

helpMemoryTips.title: 在 alone = to be at
helpMemoryTips.text: With no other verb, 在 IS the verb: 他在家 he's home, 你在哪儿? where are you?

quizzes.title: Listening: 你几点起床?
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Listen for the times — they always come right before the action they schedule.

helpMemoryTips.title: Numbers first
helpMemoryTips.text: Catch 七点, 七点半, 八点, 十二点 — pin each time to the verb that follows it and the whole story falls into place.

quizzes.readingPassage: 汤姆每天早上七点起床。他七点半喝咖啡，吃面包。八点他去学校学习中文。他很喜欢他的中文课。十二点他和小美在学校吃午饭。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng. Tā qī diǎn bàn hē kāfēi, chī miànbāo. Bā diǎn tā qù xuéxiào xuéxí Zhōngwén. Tā hěn xǐhuan tā de Zhōngwén kè. Shí'èr diǎn tā hé Xiǎoměi zài xuéxiào chī wǔfàn.

Tom gets up at seven every morning. At 7:30 he drinks coffee and eats bread. At eight he goes to school to study Chinese. He really likes his Chinese class. At twelve he and Xiaomei eat lunch at school.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆几点起床？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What time does Tom get up?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆早上喝什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom drink in the morning?

readingQuestions.question: 他和谁吃午饭？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does he eat lunch with?

quizzes.title: Going to do: 去 + verb

subjects.display: He goes to school to study Chinese.
She is coming to see you. (come see)
Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to see a friend.
Do you want to go buy books?

sentences.sentence: I'm going to buy coffee. → 我____咖啡。
He goes to school to study Chinese. → 他去学校____中文。
sentences.english: He goes to school to study Chinese.

sentences.sentence: We're going to eat. (go eat-rice) → 我们____。
She is coming to see you. (come see) → 她____你。
sentences.english: She is coming to see you. (come see)

sentences.sentence: Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to see a friend. → 明天我去北京____朋友。
sentences.hint: míngtiān wǒ qù Běijīng kàn péngyou
sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to see a friend.

sentences.sentence: Do you want to go buy books? → 你想____书吗？
sentences.hint: nǐ xiǎng qù mǎi shū ma
sentences.english: Do you want to go buy books?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Verbs chain directly in Chinese: 去买咖啡 = go buy coffee. No "to", no linking word — the second verb is the purpose of the first.

helpMemoryTips.title: Verbs stack bare (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我去学校学习中文 — go + study, no connector. English needs "to"; Chinese just lines the actions up in order of happening.

quizzes.title: Wanting: 想 / 要

subjects.display: I would like to drink tea.
I want a cup of coffee. (ordering)
He would like to go to China.
Do you want to watch TV?
We are going to buy a computer. (firm plan)

sentences.sentence: I would like to drink tea. → 我____喝茶。
sentences.english: I would like to drink tea.

sentences.sentence: I want a cup of coffee. (ordering) → 我____一杯咖啡。
sentences.english: I want a cup of coffee. (ordering)

sentences.sentence: He would like to go to China. → 他____去中国。
sentences.english: He would like to go to China.

sentences.sentence: Do you want to watch TV? → 你____看电视吗？
sentences.english: Do you want to watch TV?

sentences.sentence: We are going to buy a computer. (firm plan) → 我们____买电脑。
sentences.english: We are going to buy a computer. (firm plan)

sentences.sentence: I miss my mum. → 我____我妈妈。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 想 xiǎng = would like to (soft), 要 yào = want / am going to (firm). Both sit directly before the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: 想 wishes, 要 orders
helpMemoryTips.text: 我想喝茶 I feel like tea; 我要喝茶 I WANT tea / I'm having tea. In a café, 我要一杯咖啡 is how you actually order.

helpMemoryTips.title: 想 + noun = to miss
helpMemoryTips.text: 我想你 = I miss you — 想 straight onto a person means missing them, not wanting them to do something.

quizzes.title: Can: 会 / 能 / 可以

sentences.sentence: I can speak Chinese. (learned skill) → 我____说中文。
She can't cook. (never learned) → 她不____做饭。
I can't come today. (circumstances) → 我今天不____来。
May I sit here? (permission) → 我____坐这儿吗？
Can you swim? (skill) → 你____游泳吗？
You may drink tea here. (allowed) → 你____在这儿喝茶。
sentences.hint: nǐ kěyǐ zài zhèr hē chá

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: English "can" splits three ways: 会 = learned skill, 能 = physically/circumstantially able, 可以 = allowed.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Skill 会, power 能, permission 可以 (Z26)
helpMemoryTips.text: Learned it? 会 (我会说中文). Able right now? 能 (今天我不能来). Allowed? 可以 (这儿可以坐吗?). Pick by asking WHY you "can".

helpMemoryTips.title: 会 also predicts
helpMemoryTips.text: Later, 会 marks likely futures: 明天会下雨 — it will rain. Skill first, forecast later.

quizzes.title: Reading: 汤姆的一天
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A full day, scheduled the Chinese way: every time and place stands before its verb. Read it twice — once for the story, once for the word order.

helpMemoryTips.title: Spot the pattern (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: Underline mentally: 七点起床, 在学校学习, 晚上六点回家 — WHEN/WHERE + verb, sentence after sentence. That rhythm is the grammar.

quizzes.readingPassage: 汤姆每天早上七点起床，七点半喝咖啡。八点他去学校，在学校学习中文。十二点他和朋友吃午饭。下午他在图书馆看书。晚上六点他回家做饭。他会做英国菜，可是他更想学做中国菜。晚上他有时候看电视，有时候给妈妈打电话。他十一点睡觉。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng, qī diǎn bàn hē kāfēi. Bā diǎn tā qù xuéxiào, zài xuéxiào xuéxí Zhōngwén. Shí'èr diǎn tā hé péngyou chī wǔfàn. Xiàwǔ tā zài túshūguǎn kàn shū. Wǎnshang liù diǎn tā huí jiā zuòfàn. Tā huì zuò Yīngguó cài, kěshì tā gèng xiǎng xué zuò Zhōngguó cài. Wǎnshang tā yǒushíhou kàn diànshì, yǒushíhou gěi māma dǎ diànhuà. Tā shíyī diǎn shuìjiào.

Tom gets up at seven every morning and drinks coffee at 7:30. At eight he goes to school, where he studies Chinese. At twelve he eats lunch with friends. In the afternoon he reads in the library. At six in the evening he goes home and cooks. He can cook British food, but he'd rather learn to cook Chinese food. In the evening he sometimes watches TV, sometimes phones his mum. He goes to bed at eleven.

readingQuestions.question: 下午他做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does he do in the afternoon?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想学做什么菜？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What food does Tom want to learn to cook?

quizzes.title: Sounds: -n vs -ng, j/q/x, ü

subjects.english: j q x: jiā qī xiǎo — home, seven, small
ü after j/q/x: qù jǔ xǔ
Wǒ xiǎng qù Zhōngguó. — I'd like to go to China.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Three sound contrasts English ears blur: the -n/-ng endings, the smiling j/q/x row, and ü. Exaggerate them now, relax later.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ fán ≠ fáng (Z5)
helpMemoryTips.text: -n ends with the tongue tip at the teeth; -ng ends open, in the throat. 半 bàn vs 帮 bāng, 人 rén vs 冷 lěng — different words.

helpMemoryTips.title: ü = "ee" with rounded lips
helpMemoryTips.text: Say "ee", freeze your tongue, round your lips: 去 qù, 女 nǚ, 绿 lǜ. After j/q/x it's written u but still sounds ü.

quizzes.title: Daily verbs
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The verbs of an ordinary day. Several are verb+object pairs (吃饭 eat-rice, 睡觉 sleep-a-sleep) — learn them as one word for now.

helpMemoryTips.title: Verb + built-in object
helpMemoryTips.text: 吃饭, 睡觉, 上班, 打电话 carry a default object inside. Later you'll split them (睡了一个好觉) — for now treat each as a unit.

quizzes.title: 每天 / 常常 / 有时候

subjects.display: He often goes to the library.
She gets up at six every day.

sentences.sentence: I drink coffee every day. → 我____喝咖啡。
He often goes to the library. → 他____去图书馆。
sentences.english: He often goes to the library.

sentences.sentence: Sometimes I watch TV. → 我____看电视。
She gets up at six every day. → 她____六点起床。
sentences.english: She gets up at six every day.

sentences.sentence: We often eat at home. → 我们____在家吃饭。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: How often? 每天 every day, 常常 often, 有时候 sometimes — all take the time slot before the verb, like every other time word.

helpMemoryTips.title: Frequency lives in the WHEN slot (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我常常喝茶, 他每天上班 — same position as 明天 or 七点. One slot to rule all time words.

quizzes.title: Dictation: my routine

subjects.english: I get up at seven every day.
I'd like to go to China.

subjects.display: 我有时候在咖啡馆看书。
subjects.english: Sometimes I read at the café.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear. The times and places all come before their verbs — let the word order guide your typing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Homophone alert: diǎn
helpMemoryTips.text: Typing "qidiǎn"? 七点 (7 o'clock) — the IME may offer 起点 (starting point). Context beats the first suggestion.

quizzes.title: Reading: 在咖啡馆
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Your first dialogue. Notice how the answer to a Chinese question keeps the question's exact shape — 能…吗? → 能!

helpMemoryTips.title: Answer with the verb
helpMemoryTips.text: Chinese has no yes/no words: answer by echoing the verb. 能吗? → 能 / 不能. 想去吗? → 想 / 不想.

quizzes.readingPassage:
星期六早上，汤姆和小美在咖啡馆。
小美："你想喝什么？"
汤姆："我要一杯咖啡。你呢？"
小美："我不喝咖啡，我要一杯茶。"
汤姆："你今天下午想做什么？"
小美："我想去书店买书，你能和我一起去吗？"
汤姆："能！我也想买一本中文书。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Xīngqīliù zǎoshang, Tāngmǔ hé Xiǎoměi zài kāfēiguǎn.
Xiǎoměi: "Nǐ xiǎng hē shénme?"
Tāngmǔ: "Wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi. Nǐ ne?"
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ bù hē kāfēi, wǒ yào yì bēi chá."
Tāngmǔ: "Nǐ jīntiān xiàwǔ xiǎng zuò shénme?"
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ xiǎng qù shūdiàn mǎi shū, nǐ néng hé wǒ yìqǐ qù ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Néng! Wǒ yě xiǎng mǎi yì běn Zhōngwén shū."

Saturday morning, Tom and Xiaomei are at the café.
Xiaomei: "What would you like to drink?"
Tom: "I'll have a coffee. You?"
Xiaomei: "I don't drink coffee — I'll have a tea."
Tom: "What do you want to do this afternoon?"
Xiaomei: "I'd like to go to the bookshop to buy books. Can you come with me?"
Tom: "I can! I'd like to buy a Chinese book too."

readingQuestions.question: 小美下午想去哪儿？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Where does Xiaomei want to go in the afternoon?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想买什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom want to buy?

quizzes.title: Listening: 周末做什么?
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Xiaomei's weekend. Listen once for the days, once for what happens on each.

helpMemoryTips.title: Weekend = 周末
helpMemoryTips.text: 周 is the formal "week": 周末 weekend, 周一 = 星期一 Monday. You'll hear both systems everywhere.

quizzes.readingPassage: 我周末不上课。星期六早上我常常去咖啡馆看书。下午我喜欢和朋友去公园。星期天我在家。早上我给妈妈打电话，下午我做饭。我会做很多中国菜。晚上我有时候看电视，十点半睡觉。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Wǒ zhōumò bú shàngkè. Xīngqīliù zǎoshang wǒ chángcháng qù kāfēiguǎn kàn shū. Xiàwǔ wǒ xǐhuan hé péngyou qù gōngyuán. Xīngqītiān wǒ zài jiā. Zǎoshang wǒ gěi māma dǎ diànhuà, xiàwǔ wǒ zuòfàn. Wǒ huì zuò hěn duō Zhōngguó cài. Wǎnshang wǒ yǒushíhou kàn diànshì, shí diǎn bàn shuìjiào.

I don't have class at the weekend. On Saturday morning I often go to the café to read. In the afternoon I like going to the park with friends. On Sunday I stay home. In the morning I phone my mum; in the afternoon I cook. I can make lots of Chinese dishes. In the evening I sometimes watch TV, and I go to bed at half past ten.

readingQuestions.question: 星期六早上小美常常做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Xiaomei often do on Saturday morning?

readingQuestions.question: 星期天早上她给谁打电话？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does she phone on Sunday morning?

readingQuestions.question: 她几点睡觉？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What time does she go to bed?

quizzes.title: 了 №1 — the action is done

subjects.display: He drank two cups of coffee.
Yesterday I was very busy. (state — NO 了!)
I drink tea every day. (habit — NO 了!)

sentences.sentence: I bought a book. → 我买____一本书。
sentences.hint: wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū

sentences.sentence: He drank two cups of coffee. → 他喝____两杯咖啡。
sentences.hint: tā hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi
sentences.english: He drank two cups of coffee.

sentences.sentence: We ate lunch. → 我们吃____午饭。
She went to Beijing yesterday. → 她昨天去____北京。
Yesterday I was very busy. (state — NO 了!) → 昨天我____忙。
sentences.english: Yesterday I was very busy. (state — NO 了!)

sentences.sentence: I drink tea every day. (habit — NO 了!) → 我____喝茶。
sentences.english: I drink tea every day. (habit — NO 了!)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 了 stamps an action as completed: 我买了一本书 — I bought a book. It's a ✓-stamp, not a past tense: habits and states never take it.

helpMemoryTips.title: A ✓-stamp, not a tense (Z14)
helpMemoryTips.text: Ask "did the action complete?" — if yes, stamp the verb: 吃了, 买了, 去了. If you're describing a habit or a state, no stamp.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Past ≠ 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 昨天我很忙 (yesterday I was busy) has NO 了 — 忙 is a state, nothing completed. 每天…了 ✗ too: habits aren't single completed events. This is the #1 error at every level.

quizzes.title: 了 №2 — the situation is new

subjects.display: He is a doctor now. (he wasn't before)
It's twelve o'clock — time to eat!
My younger sister is tall now.

sentences.sentence: I'm tired (I've gotten tired). → 我累____。
He is a doctor now. (he wasn't before) → 他是医生____。
sentences.english: He is a doctor now. (he wasn't before)

sentences.sentence: I don't drink coffee anymore. → 我不喝咖啡____。
It's twelve o'clock — time to eat! → 十二点____，吃饭吧！
sentences.english: It's twelve o'clock — time to eat!

sentences.sentence: My younger sister is tall now. → 我妹妹高____。
sentences.english: My younger sister is tall now.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Sentence-final 了 stamps a CHANGE: 下雨了 — it's raining (now); 我累了 — I've gotten tired. Something is different from before.

helpMemoryTips.title: End-of-sentence 了 = "new now" (Z14)
helpMemoryTips.text: 他是学生了 — he's a student NOW (he wasn't). 我不喝咖啡了 — I don't drink coffee ANYMORE. The 了 says: update your picture.

helpMemoryTips.title: Two 了s, two jobs
helpMemoryTips.text: Verb-了 = action completed (买了). Sentence-了 = situation changed (下雨了). One character, two stamps — context tells you which.

quizzes.title: Didn't: 没(有) — and the 不/没 split

subjects.display: We haven't eaten yet. (not yet: 还没)
I didn't watch TV last night.

sentences.sentence: I didn't buy the book. → 我____买书。
He didn't come yesterday. → 他昨天____来。
We haven't eaten yet. (not yet: 还没) → 我们____吃饭。
sentences.english: We haven't eaten yet. (not yet: 还没)

sentences.sentence: I don't drink coffee. (habit → 不) → 我____喝咖啡。
She isn't going tomorrow. (future → 不) → 她明天____去。
I didn't watch TV last night. → 我昨天晚上____看电视。
sentences.hint: wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang méi kàn diànshì
sentences.english: I didn't watch TV last night.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: To say something DIDN'T happen, use 没(有) before the verb — and drop the 了: 我没买书. 不 keeps its jobs: habits, futures, states.

helpMemoryTips.title: 没 for done-and-have, 不 for everything else (Z17)
helpMemoryTips.text: 没 negates completed events (没去 didn't go) and 有. 不 negates habits (不喝咖啡), futures (明天不去), adjectives (不累) and willingness.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 没 kills the 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我没买了书 ✗ — once 没 says "not completed", the ✓-stamp 了 must go: 我没买书. They never appear together.

quizzes.title: Speaking: what I did yesterday

subjects.english: Zuótiān wǒ liù diǎn qǐchuáng. — Yesterday I got up at six.
Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū. — I bought a book.
Wǒ hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi. — I drank two coffees.
Wǎnshang wǒ méi kàn diànshì. — I didn't watch TV in the evening.
Zuótiān wǒ hěn máng. — Yesterday I was very busy. (no 了!)
Wǒ shí diǎn jiù shuìjiào le. — I went to bed at ten already.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tell yesterday's story aloud. Feel where 了 lands — and where it doesn't.

helpMemoryTips.title: Stamp as you speak
helpMemoryTips.text: As you repeat, mentally tick each completed action at its 了: 起床✓, 买了✓… The state sentences (很忙, 很累) get no tick — hear the difference (Z14).

quizzes.title: Ever done: 过

subjects.display: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?
She has never been to Britain.
He has never drunk Chinese tea.

sentences.sentence: I have been to China. → 我去____中国。
Have you ever eaten Peking duck? → 你吃____北京烤鸭吗？
sentences.hint: nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma
sentences.english: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?

sentences.sentence: She has never been to Britain. → 她____去过英国。
sentences.english: She has never been to Britain.

sentences.sentence: We have seen this film. → 我们看____这个电影。
sentences.hint: wǒmen kàn guo zhè ge diànyǐng

sentences.sentence: I have studied Chinese before. → 我学____中文。
He has never drunk Chinese tea. → 他没喝____中国茶。
sentences.hint: tā méi hē guo Zhōngguó chá
sentences.english: He has never drunk Chinese tea.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 过 guo marks life experience: 我去过中国 — I've been to China (at some point). Negate with 没…过 — and the 过 stays!

helpMemoryTips.title: 过 = the passport stamp (Z15)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了 stamps ONE completed event; 过 stamps your passport: "this experience exists in my life". 你吃过北京烤鸭吗? — Have you ever had Peking duck?

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 没 keeps 过 (unlike 了)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我没去过中国 — the 过 survives negation: "the experience is missing". Compare 我没买书, where 了 disappears.

quizzes.title: Listening: 你吃饭了吗?
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 你吃饭了吗? is also a classic Chinese greeting. Listen for 了, 过 and 还没 doing their different jobs.

helpMemoryTips.title: The greeting that isn't a question
helpMemoryTips.text: 你吃了吗? between neighbours just means "hi". Here it's a real question — context decides.

quizzes.readingPassage:
小美："汤姆，你吃午饭了吗？"
汤姆："还没呢。我早上只喝了一杯咖啡。"
小美："我知道一个很好的饭馆。你吃过中国菜吗？"
汤姆："吃过，可是我没吃过北京烤鸭。"
小美："那我们今天去吃烤鸭吧！"
汤姆："太好了！我们走吧。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Xiǎoměi: "Tāngmǔ, nǐ chī wǔfàn le ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Hái méi ne. Wǒ zǎoshang zhǐ hē le yì bēi kāfēi."
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ zhīdào yí ge hěn hǎo de fànguǎn. Nǐ chī guo Zhōngguó cài ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Chī guo, kěshì wǒ méi chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā."
Xiǎoměi: "Nà wǒmen jīntiān qù chī kǎoyā ba!"
Tāngmǔ: "Tài hǎo le! Wǒmen zǒu ba."

Xiaomei: "Tom, have you had lunch?"
Tom: "Not yet. I only had a coffee this morning."
Xiaomei: "I know a great restaurant. Have you ever had Chinese food?"
Tom: "I have — but I've never had Peking duck."
Xiaomei: "Then let's go eat duck today!"
Tom: "Great! Let's go."

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆早上喝了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Tom drink in the morning?

quizzes.title: The measure-word system

sentences.sentence: a (flat) photo (flat → 张) → 一____照片
a (long) road (long & bendy → 条) → 一____路
a bottle of water → 一____水
a shirt (clothes-top → 件) → 一____衬衫
a pair of shoes (pairs → 双) → 一____鞋
two teachers (polite → 位) → 两____老师

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Beyond 个: nouns sort by shape and kind. 本 for bound things, 张 for flat things, 条 for long bendy things, 只 for animals, 杯 cups, 瓶 bottles, 件 clothes-tops, 双 pairs, 辆 vehicles, 位 people (polite).

helpMemoryTips.title: Sort by shape (Z11)
helpMemoryTips.text: Bound pages → 本. Flat sheet → 张. Long & bendy → 条. On legs → 只. Politely human → 位. When truly lost, 个 still works — but each right suitcase earns you fluency points.

helpMemoryTips.title: English does this too
helpMemoryTips.text: A PAIR of trousers, a SHEET of paper, a CUP of tea — English partitives are measure words in disguise. Chinese just applies them to every noun.

quizzes.title: Shopping: 多少钱 / 块 / 毛

subjects.display: A little cheaper, OK? (cheap: 便宜)
I want to buy this shirt.
Do you sell tea? (sell: 卖 — mind the tone!)

sentences.sentence: How much is this? → 这个____？
A little cheaper, OK? (cheap: 便宜) → ____一点儿，好吗？
sentences.english: A little cheaper, OK? (cheap: 便宜)

sentences.sentence: I want to buy this shirt. → 我想____这件衬衫。
sentences.hint: wǒ xiǎng mǎi zhè jiàn chènshān
sentences.english: I want to buy this shirt.

sentences.sentence: Do you sell tea? (sell: 卖 — mind the tone!) → 你们____茶吗？
sentences.english: Do you sell tea? (sell: 卖 — mind the tone!)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Money talk: 多少钱? how much? Prices come in 块 kuài (yuan) and 毛 máo (tenths). Too expensive? 太贵了!

helpMemoryTips.title: 太…了 = way too …
helpMemoryTips.text: 太贵了! too expensive! 太好了! great! The 太…了 sandwich turns any adjective up to eleven.

helpMemoryTips.title: 块 on the street, 元 on the receipt
helpMemoryTips.text: Spoken prices use 块 (and 毛 for tenths); written prices use 元/角. 二十五块五 = ¥25.50.

quizzes.title: Reading: 买东西
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tom haggles. Track the measure words (件, 瓶) and the money — and note 零 in 一百零六 (one hundred **and** six).

helpMemoryTips.title: 零 plugs the gap
helpMemoryTips.text: 106 = 一百零六 — the 零 (zero) marks the skipped tens place. 160 would be 一百六(十).

quizzes.readingPassage:
今天下午汤姆去商店买东西。他想买一件衬衫。
汤姆："你好，这件白色的衬衫多少钱？"
售货员："一百二十块。"
汤姆："太贵了！能便宜一点儿吗？"
售货员："一百块，怎么样？"
汤姆："好，我买了。我还要两瓶水。"
售货员："一共一百零六块。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Jīntiān xiàwǔ Tāngmǔ qù shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi. Tā xiǎng mǎi yí jiàn chènshān.
Tāngmǔ: "Nǐ hǎo, zhè jiàn báisè de chènshān duōshao qián?"
Shòuhuòyuán: "Yìbǎi èrshí kuài."
Tāngmǔ: "Tài guì le! Néng piányi yìdiǎnr ma?"
Shòuhuòyuán: "Yìbǎi kuài, zěnmeyàng?"
Tāngmǔ: "Hǎo, wǒ mǎi le. Wǒ hái yào liǎng píng shuǐ."
Shòuhuòyuán: "Yígòng yìbǎi líng liù kuài."

This afternoon Tom goes shopping. He wants to buy a shirt.
Tom: "Hello, how much is this white shirt?"
Shop assistant: "120 kuai."
Tom: "Too expensive! Can you make it a bit cheaper?"
Assistant: "100 kuai — how about that?"
Tom: "OK, I'll take it. I also want two bottles of water."
Assistant: "Altogether 106 kuai."

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想买什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom want to buy?

readingQuestions.question: 衬衫多少钱？（最后）
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How much is the shirt (in the end)?

quizzes.title: Comparing with 比

subjects.display: This shirt is more expensive than that one.
Beijing is a bit colder than Shanghai. (a bit: 一点儿 after adj)
Tea is much cheaper than coffee. (much: 得多)
My older brother is busier than me.
I am not as tall as him.

sentences.sentence: He is taller than me. → 他____我高。
This shirt is more expensive than that one. → 这件衬衫____那件贵。
sentences.hint: zhè jiàn chènshān bǐ nà jiàn guì
sentences.english: This shirt is more expensive than that one.

sentences.sentence: Beijing is a bit colder than Shanghai. (a bit: 一点儿 after adj) → 北京比上海冷____。
sentences.english: Beijing is a bit colder than Shanghai. (a bit: 一点儿 after adj)

sentences.sentence: Tea is much cheaper than coffee. (much: 得多) → 茶比咖啡便宜____。
sentences.hint: chá bǐ kāfēi piányi de duō
sentences.english: Tea is much cheaper than coffee. (much: 得多)

sentences.sentence: My older brother is busier than me. → 我哥哥____我忙。
sentences.english: My older brother is busier than me.

sentences.sentence: I am not as tall as him. → 我____他高。
sentences.english: I am not as tall as him.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A 比 B + adjective: 他比我高 — he (compared-to me) is tall(er). No "-er", no "more" — and crucially, no 很.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ A 比 B tall — and never 很 (Z24)
helpMemoryTips.text: 他比我**很**高 ✗. Degree goes AFTER the adjective instead: 高一点儿 a bit taller, 高得多 much taller.

helpMemoryTips.title: Compare the other way: 没有
helpMemoryTips.text: B 没有 A 高 = B isn't as tall as A. The negative of a 比-sentence flips to 没有…那么/这么.

quizzes.title: 一点儿 vs 有点儿

sentences.sentence: This is a bit expensive. (complaint) → 这个____贵。
A bit cheaper, please. (request) → 便宜____。
I'm a bit tired. → 我____累。
Drink a little water. → 喝____水。
Today is a bit cold. → 今天____冷。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Both mean "a little" — but 一点儿 follows adjectives/nouns (便宜一点儿, 一点儿水), while 有点儿 goes before adjectives and always complains: 有点儿贵.

helpMemoryTips.title: 有点儿 = "a bit too…" (complaint)
helpMemoryTips.text: 这个有点儿贵 — hmm, a bit pricey (negative feel). 便宜一点儿 — a bit cheaper please (request). Before = feeling, after = amount.

quizzes.title: Sounds: 不 & 一 change tone

subjects.english: bú shì, bú qù, bú lèi — 不 before 4th tones
bù gāo, bù máng, bù hǎo — 不 stays bù
yí ge, yí jiàn, yí wèi — 一 before 4th tones
yì bēi, yì píng, yì běn — 一 before tones 1/2/3
Wǒ bú shì lǎoshī. — I'm not a teacher.

subjects.display: 我买了一件衬衫和一双鞋。
subjects.english: Wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn chènshān hé yì shuāng xié. — I bought a shirt and a pair of shoes.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Two everyday words bend their tone: 不 bù → bú before a 4th tone, and 一 yī → yí before a 4th, yì before the rest. Say them until it's automatic.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 不 flips before a fall (Z2)
helpMemoryTips.text: bù + 4th → bú: 不是 bú shì, 不去 bú qù, 不累 bú lèi. Everywhere else it stays bù: 不高, 不忙, 不喝.

helpMemoryTips.title: 一 has three faces
helpMemoryTips.text: Counting: yī (一, 十一). Before a 4th tone: yí (一件, 一个*). Before tones 1/2/3: yì (一杯, 一瓶, 一本). *个 counts as 4th.

quizzes.title: Food & drink
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The essentials for menus and markets — with their measure words attached where it helps.

helpMemoryTips.title: 菜 = dish, not just vegetable
helpMemoryTips.text: 中国菜 Chinese food, 做菜 to cook — 菜 covers whole cuisines. 米饭 is the cooked rice on your plate.

quizzes.title: Dictation: yesterday

subjects.english: Have you ever been to China?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear — every 了, 过 and 没 included. They're short, unstressed and easy to drop: that's exactly why we drill them.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Listen for the small words (Z14/Z15)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了, 过, 没, 还 carry the whole meaning of the sentence. If your typed line misses one, the sentence changed tense — er, aspect.

quizzes.title: Reading: 汤姆的周末
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The whole module in one story: 了 for completed actions, 过 for experiences, 没…过 for the ones still missing.

helpMemoryTips.title: Three stamps, one story
helpMemoryTips.text: 买了 (done), 没吃过 (experience missing), 还没去过 (still not yet). Find each in the text and say why it's not the others.

quizzes.readingPassage: 上个周末汤姆很忙。星期六早上他去了商店，买了一件衬衫和一双鞋。下午他和小美去饭馆吃了北京烤鸭。汤姆以前没吃过烤鸭，他觉得太好吃了！星期天他在家学习中文，晚上给妈妈打了电话。妈妈问："你去过长城吗？"汤姆说："还没去过，我下个月想去。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Shàng ge zhōumò Tāngmǔ hěn máng. Xīngqīliù zǎoshang tā qù le shāngdiàn, mǎi le yí jiàn chènshān hé yì shuāng xié. Xiàwǔ tā hé Xiǎoměi qù fànguǎn chī le Běijīng kǎoyā. Tāngmǔ yǐqián méi chī guo kǎoyā, tā juéde tài hǎochī le! Xīngqītiān tā zài jiā xuéxí Zhōngwén, wǎnshang gěi māma dǎ le diànhuà. Māma wèn: "Nǐ qù guo Chángchéng ma?" Tāngmǔ shuō: "Hái méi qù guo, wǒ xià ge yuè xiǎng qù."

Last weekend Tom was busy. On Saturday morning he went to the shops and bought a shirt and a pair of shoes. In the afternoon he and Xiaomei ate Peking duck at a restaurant. Tom had never had roast duck before — he thought it was delicious! On Sunday he studied Chinese at home, and in the evening he phoned his mum. Mum asked: "Have you been to the Great Wall?" Tom said: "Not yet — I'd like to go next month."

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆星期六买了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Tom buy on Saturday?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆以前吃过烤鸭吗？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Had Tom eaten roast duck before?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆什么时候想去长城？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When would Tom like to go to the Great Wall?

quizzes.title: Verbs need a landing: 完 / 到 / 懂

subjects.display: He bought (managed to get) the ticket.

sentences.sentence: I finished reading this book. → 我看____了这本书。
sentences.hint: wǒ kàn wán le zhè běn shū

sentences.sentence: I found my phone! → 我找____了我的手机！
sentences.hint: wǒ zhǎo dào le wǒ de shǒujī

sentences.sentence: Did you understand (by listening)? → 你听____了吗？
We finished eating. → 我们吃____了。
I understood this book. (by reading) → 我看____了这本书。
sentences.hint: wǒ kàn dǒng le zhè běn shū

sentences.sentence: He bought (managed to get) the ticket. → 他买____了票。
sentences.english: He bought (managed to get) the ticket.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 找 is to look — 找到 is to find. Chinese verbs describe the attempt; a result complement lands them: 完 finished, 到 attained, 懂 understood.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Verb + landing (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: English packs result into the verb (find, hear); Chinese splits it: 找 look + 到 = find; 听 listen + 懂 = understand (by ear); 吃 eat + 完 = finish eating.

helpMemoryTips.title: The landing takes the 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我看完了这本书 — the ✓-stamp follows the whole verb+landing unit: 看完了, 找到了, 听懂了.

quizzes.title: More landings: 见 / 好 / 错 — and 没 V 完

subjects.display: I haven't finished my homework yet.
Sorry, you've called the wrong number.

sentences.sentence: I saw him. (see = look + register) → 我看____他了。
I didn't hear (register) it. → 我没听____。
The food is ready. (done-and-good) → 饭做____了。
You wrote this character wrongly. → 你写____了这个字。
sentences.hint: nǐ xiě cuò le zhè ge zì

sentences.sentence: I haven't finished my homework yet. → 我还____做完作业。
sentences.hint: wǒ hái méi zuò wán zuòyè
sentences.english: I haven't finished my homework yet.

sentences.sentence: Sorry, you've called the wrong number. → 对不起，你打____了。
sentences.english: Sorry, you've called the wrong number.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 见 registers perception (看见 see, 听见 hear), 好 means done-and-ready, 错 means wrongly. Negate a missed result with 没: 我没听懂.

helpMemoryTips.title: 没 + verb + landing (Z21/Z17)
helpMemoryTips.text: The result didn't happen → 没, and the 了 goes: 我没看见他 I didn't see him; 我还没做完 I'm not done yet.

helpMemoryTips.title: 错 = did it, but wrongly
helpMemoryTips.text: 我说错了 I misspoke; 你打错了 wrong number. The action happened — the landing says it went wrong.

quizzes.title: Speaking: verb + landing drills

subjects.english: Wǒ zhǎo dào le! — I found it!
Wǒ tīng dǒng le. — I understood (hearing it).
Wǒ hái méi kàn wán. — I haven't finished reading it.
Fàn zuò hǎo le, chīfàn ba! — Food's ready, let's eat!
Duìbuqǐ, wǒ shuō cuò le. — Sorry, I said it wrong.
Nǐ kàn jiàn wǒ de yàoshi le ma? — Have you seen my keys?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Drill the verb-landing pairs aloud until they feel like single words — because to a Chinese ear, they are.

helpMemoryTips.title: Stress the landing
helpMemoryTips.text: The complement carries the news: 找到了! (FOUND it), 听懂了! (GOT it). Let your voice land on the landing (Z21).

quizzes.title: Direction: verb + 来 / 去

subjects.display: Please bring the tea over (here). (拿 = carry)
He went upstairs. (up + away from me, downstairs)
Tom went back home. (place in the middle!)

sentences.sentence: He went out. (exit + away) → 他____了。
Please bring the tea over (here). (拿 = carry) → 请把茶____。
sentences.english: Please bring the tea over (here). (拿 = carry)

sentences.sentence: He went upstairs. (up + away from me, downstairs) → 他____了。
sentences.english: He went upstairs. (up + away from me, downstairs)

sentences.sentence: Tom went back home. (place in the middle!) → 汤姆____了。
sentences.english: Tom went back home. (place in the middle!)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 来 = toward me, 去 = away from me. Glued after motion verbs they give English's "in/out/up/back": 进来 come in, 出去 go out, 回来 come back.

helpMemoryTips.title: The speaker is the compass (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: Every direction is measured from where YOU stand: 上来 up (toward me), 上去 up (away). Change where you stand and 来/去 swap.

helpMemoryTips.title: Places squeeze in the middle
helpMemoryTips.text: With a place, it slots before 来/去: 回家去, 进教室来 — never after: 回去家 ✗.

quizzes.title: Listening: 去医院
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tom gets sick. Listen for the landings — 听懂了, 好点儿了, 好多了 — they carry the story's progress.

helpMemoryTips.title: 好点儿了 / 好多了
helpMemoryTips.text: Recovery in two sizes: 好(一)点儿了 a bit better, 好多了 much better — comparison + change-了 in one phrase.

quizzes.readingPassage: 汤姆早上起床的时候，觉得头很疼。他没去上课，去了医院。医生看了看，说："你感冒了。回家好好休息，多喝水，吃这个药。"汤姆听懂了医生的话，买了药就回家了。下午小美打电话问他："你好点儿了吗？"汤姆说："好多了，谢谢！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ zǎoshang qǐchuáng de shíhou, juéde tóu hěn téng. Tā méi qù shàngkè, qù le yīyuàn. Yīshēng kàn le kàn, shuō: "Nǐ gǎnmào le. Huí jiā hǎohāo xiūxi, duō hē shuǐ, chī zhè ge yào." Tāngmǔ tīng dǒng le yīshēng de huà, mǎi le yào jiù huí jiā le. Xiàwǔ Xiǎoměi dǎ diànhuà wèn tā: "Nǐ hǎo diǎnr le ma?" Tāngmǔ shuō: "Hǎo duō le, xièxie!"

When Tom got up in the morning, his head hurt. He didn't go to class — he went to the hospital. The doctor had a look and said: "You've caught a cold. Go home and rest properly, drink lots of water, take this medicine." Tom understood the doctor, bought the medicine and went straight home. In the afternoon Xiaomei phoned to ask: "Are you feeling a bit better?" Tom said: "Much better, thanks!"

readingQuestions.question: 医生让汤姆做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does the doctor tell Tom to do?

readingQuestions.question: 下午汤姆怎么样了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How is Tom in the afternoon?

quizzes.title: Duration AFTER the verb

subjects.display: I studied Chinese for three years.
She lived in Beijing for two years.
I've been studying Chinese for a year (and counting).
How long did you watch TV?

sentences.sentence: I studied Chinese for three years. → 我学了____中文。
sentences.hint: wǒ xué le sān nián Zhōngwén
sentences.english: I studied Chinese for three years.

sentences.sentence: He slept for ten hours. → 他睡了____。
sentences.hint: tā shuì le shí ge xiǎoshí

sentences.sentence: We waited for twenty minutes. → 我们等了____。
She lived in Beijing for two years. → 她在北京住了____。
sentences.hint: tā zài Běijīng zhù le liǎng nián
sentences.english: She lived in Beijing for two years.

sentences.sentence: I've been studying Chinese for a year (and counting). → 我学中文学了一年____。
sentences.hint: wǒ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le
sentences.english: I've been studying Chinese for a year (and counting).

sentences.sentence: How long did you watch TV? → 你看了____电视？
sentences.hint: nǐ kàn le duō cháng shíjiān diànshì
sentences.english: How long did you watch TV?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: When something happens goes BEFORE the verb; how long it lasts goes AFTER: 我学了三年中文 — I studied Chinese for three years.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ WHEN before, HOW-LONG after (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我昨天(when)睡了十个小时(how long). Point in time = scene-setting → front. Amount of time = result-like → after the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Still going on? Double 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我学了三年了 — the second 了 says the three years reach into now: "…and counting". One 了 = a closed chapter.

quizzes.title: 的 / 得 / 地 — one sound, three jobs

subjects.display: He speaks (Chinese) very well. (grade the verb)
She walked over slowly. (style the verb)

sentences.sentence: my Chinese teacher (description + noun) → 我____中文老师
He speaks (Chinese) very well. (grade the verb) → 他说____很好。
sentences.english: He speaks (Chinese) very well. (grade the verb)

sentences.sentence: She walked over slowly. (style the verb) → 她慢慢____走过来。
sentences.english: She walked over slowly. (style the verb)

sentences.sentence: a very interesting book → 一本很有意思____书
sentences.hint: yì běn hěn yǒuyìsi de shū

sentences.sentence: He runs fast. (grade) → 他跑____很快。
Listen to the teacher carefully. (style) → 认真____听老师说。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: All three are pronounced de. 的 clips descriptions to nouns, 得 grades how a verb went, 地 turns adjectives into adverbs before the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ noun-的 · how-it-went-得 · how-you-do-it-地 (Z20)
helpMemoryTips.text: Before a NOUN → 的 (红色的车). After a VERB, grading it → 得 (说得很好). Before a VERB, styling it → 地 (慢慢地走). Ask what the de touches.

helpMemoryTips.title: One frame, three de
helpMemoryTips.text: 他是很好的老师 · 他教得很好 · 他认真地教 — same teacher, three different de.

quizzes.title: 得 — grading the result

subjects.display: She speaks Chinese very well. (repeat the verb)

sentences.sentence: He speaks very well. → 他说____很好。
She speaks Chinese very well. (repeat the verb) → 她说中文____很好。
sentences.hint: tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo
sentences.english: She speaks Chinese very well. (repeat the verb)

sentences.sentence: You came too late. → 你来____太晚了。
sentences.hint: nǐ lái de tài wǎn le

sentences.sentence: He writes characters beautifully. → 他写字写____很漂亮。
sentences.hint: tā xiě zì xiě de hěn piàoliang

sentences.sentence: They ate very happily. → 他们吃____很高兴。
How did you sleep? (slept how?) → 你睡____怎么样？

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 得 + evaluation is how Chinese says "well/badly/fast/late": 他说得很好. With an object, repeat the verb: 她说中文说得很好.

helpMemoryTips.title: V + O, V + 得 + grade (Z20/Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: Object in the sentence? Say the verb twice: 她**写**字**写得**很漂亮. The first verb carries the object, the second carries the grade.

quizzes.title: Reading: 学中文的路
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tom's first year — told with this module's whole toolkit: duration, landings, the three de, and one tone slip that proves why tones matter.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ wèn ≠ wěn
helpMemoryTips.text: 问 (ask, 4th tone) vs 吻 (kiss, 3rd tone) — the passage's joke is a real cautionary tale about tones (Z1).

quizzes.readingPassage: 汤姆学中文学了一年了。开始的时候，他觉得声调太难了，常常说错。有一次，他想说"我想问你"，可是说成了"我想吻你"，大家都笑了。现在他听得懂老师说的话，也看得懂简单的中文书。他每天认真地学习，写字写得越来越漂亮。王老师说："学外语就是这样：慢慢来，别怕说错。"汤姆觉得，虽然中文很难，但是他学得很开心。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le. Kāishǐ de shíhou, tā juéde shēngdiào tài nán le, chángcháng shuō cuò. Yǒu yí cì, tā xiǎng shuō "wǒ xiǎng wèn nǐ", kěshì shuō chéng le "wǒ xiǎng wěn nǐ", dàjiā dōu xiào le. Xiànzài tā tīng de dǒng lǎoshī shuō de huà, yě kàn de dǒng jiǎndān de Zhōngwén shū. Tā měitiān rènzhēn de xuéxí, xiě zì xiě de yuèláiyuè piàoliang. Wáng lǎoshī shuō: "Xué wàiyǔ jiù shì zhèyàng: mànmàn lái, bié pà shuō cuò." Tāngmǔ juéde, suīrán Zhōngwén hěn nán, dànshì tā xué de hěn kāixīn.

Tom has been learning Chinese for a year now. At the beginning he found the tones too hard and often misspoke. Once he meant to say "I want to ask you" (wèn) but said "I want to kiss you" (wěn) — everyone laughed. Now he can understand what the teacher says and read simple Chinese books. He studies conscientiously every day, and his characters look better and better. Teacher Wang says: "That's what learning a language is: take it slowly, don't fear mistakes." Tom feels that although Chinese is hard, he's learning it very happily.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆学中文学了多长时间了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How long has Tom been learning Chinese?

readingQuestions.question: 开始的时候，汤姆觉得什么太难了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Tom find too hard at the beginning?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想说"问"，说成了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Tom meant to say "ask" — what did he say instead?

quizzes.title: Keep BOTH: 因为…所以 / 虽然…但是

subjects.display: Because it was raining, (so) we didn't go out.
Although it's expensive, (but) it's very good.
Because I was sick, (so) I didn't go to class.
Although he is British, (but) he speaks Chinese very well.
Because the tickets sold out, (so) we watched TV at home.

sentences.sentence: Because it was raining, (so) we didn't go out. → 因为下雨了，____我们没出去。
sentences.hint: yīnwèi xià yǔ le, suǒyǐ wǒmen méi chūqù
sentences.english: Because it was raining, (so) we didn't go out.
sentences.referenceExample: 因为下雨了，**所以**我们没出去。

sentences.sentence: Although it's expensive, (but) it's very good. → 虽然很贵，____很好。
sentences.hint: suīrán hěn guì, dànshì hěn hǎo
sentences.english: Although it's expensive, (but) it's very good.

sentences.sentence: Because I was sick, (so) I didn't go to class. → ____我病了，所以没去上课。
sentences.hint: yīnwèi wǒ bìng le, suǒyǐ méi qù shàngkè
sentences.english: Because I was sick, (so) I didn't go to class.

sentences.sentence: Although he is British, (but) he speaks Chinese very well. → ____他是英国人，但是他中文说得很好。
sentences.hint: suīrán tā shì Yīngguó rén, dànshì tā Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo
sentences.english: Although he is British, (but) he speaks Chinese very well.
sentences.referenceExample: **虽然**他是英国人，但是他中文说得很好。

sentences.sentence: Because the tickets sold out, (so) we watched TV at home. → 因为票卖完了，____我们在家看电视。
sentences.hint: yīnwèi piào mài wán le, suǒyǐ wǒmen zài jiā kàn diànshì
sentences.english: Because the tickets sold out, (so) we watched TV at home.
sentences.referenceExample: 因为票卖完了，**所以**我们在家看电视。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Chinese connectives come in pairs and keep both halves: 因为 A，所以 B (because A, so B); 虽然 A，但是 B (although A, but B).

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't drop the second half (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: English "although" bans a following "but" — Chinese REQUIRES it: 虽然贵，**但是**很好. Dropping 但是/所以 sounds broken, not elegant.

quizzes.title: Health & body

subjects.display: to see a doctor (look at illness)

sentences.sentence: I have a headache. (head hurts) → 我____。
He has caught a cold. → 他____了。
to see a doctor (look at illness) → ____
sentences.english: to see a doctor (look at illness)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Aches, colds and the doctor. The pattern for pain: body part + 疼 — 我头疼, literally "I head-hurt".

helpMemoryTips.title: X 疼 = my X hurts
helpMemoryTips.text: 头疼 headache, 肚子疼 stomach ache — no "have a" needed: the body part is the topic and 疼 does the rest (Z28 preview).

quizzes.title: Speaking: longer sentences, steady tones

subjects.english: Wǒ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le. — I've been learning Chinese for a year.
Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de fēicháng hǎo. — She speaks Chinese extremely well.

subjects.display: 因为我病了，所以没去上课。
subjects.english: Yīnwèi wǒ bìng le, suǒyǐ méi qù shàngkè. — Because I was ill, I didn't go to class.

subjects.display: 请你慢慢地说，我听得懂。
subjects.english: Qǐng nǐ mànmàn de shuō, wǒ tīng de dǒng. — Speak slowly please, and I can understand.

subjects.display: 虽然很难，但是很有意思。
subjects.english: Suīrán hěn nán, dànshì hěn yǒuyìsi. — Hard, but interesting.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Longer sentences now — keep every syllable's tone while the sentence flows. Chinese rhythm gives each syllable its beat.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't stress-time it (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: English squeezes unstressed syllables; Chinese gives each syllable even weight. Resist rushing the "small" words — 了, 的, 得 stay clear (just lighter).

quizzes.title: Big text: 的/得/地 in a letter
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tom's letter home — with every de removed. Read it once, then choose 的, 得 or 地 for each gap: what does the de touch?

helpMemoryTips.title: The three-question test (Z20)
helpMemoryTips.text: Before a noun? → 的. After a verb, grading how it went? → 得. Before a verb, styling how it's done? → 地. Every gap answers one of the three.

quizzes.readingPassage:

quizzes.title: Listening: 王老师的建议
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Teacher Wang's three tips — a listening full of landings (学好, 说错, 写完, 写对) and both de-graders.

helpMemoryTips.title: 第 makes ordinals
helpMemoryTips.text: 第一, 第二, 第三 — first, second, third. 第 + number turns any count into a ranking.

quizzes.readingPassage: 很多学生问我，怎么才能学好中文。我想说三件事。第一，每天都要听，听得越多，懂得越多。第二，别怕说错。说错了没关系，说得多了，就说得好了。第三，认真地写汉字。写完一个字，要问自己：我写对了吗？因为学外语不容易，所以要慢慢来。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Hěn duō xuésheng wèn wǒ, zěnme cái néng xué hǎo Zhōngwén. Wǒ xiǎng shuō sān jiàn shì. Dì yī, měitiān dōu yào tīng, tīng de yuè duō, dǒng de yuè duō. Dì èr, bié pà shuō cuò. Shuō cuò le méi guānxi, shuō de duō le, jiù shuō de hǎo le. Dì sān, rènzhēn de xiě Hànzì. Xiě wán yí ge zì, yào wèn zìjǐ: wǒ xiě duì le ma? Yīnwèi xué wàiyǔ bù róngyì, suǒyǐ yào mànmàn lái.

Many students ask me how to master Chinese. I'd say three things. First, listen every day — the more you hear, the more you understand. Second, don't fear mistakes. Misspeaking doesn't matter: speak a lot and you'll speak well. Third, write characters carefully. When you finish one, ask yourself: did I write it right? Learning a language isn't easy, so take it step by step.

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What about making mistakes when speaking?

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Your IME writes all three de as "de"
helpMemoryTips.text: Typing "de" offers 的/得/地 — the sentence's grammar picks the winner, not the first suggestion (Z20).

quizzes.title: Reading: 汤姆病了
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The whole module in a story: durations (两天, 十二个小时), landings (买来), pairs (因为…所以) and a graded 得 (好得这么快).

helpMemoryTips.title: 买来 = bought & brought
helpMemoryTips.text: 买来了药 — the 来 lands the buying at Tom's door. Directional complements sneak onto ordinary verbs everywhere (Z21).

quizzes.readingPassage: 上个星期，汤姆病了。他头疼，肚子也疼，两天没去上课。小美给他买来了药和水果。她说："多休息，多喝水，你很快就会好的。"汤姆吃了药，睡了十二个小时。第二天，他觉得好多了。他给小美打电话："谢谢你！因为你的帮助，所以我好得这么快。"小美笑着说："别客气！朋友就是要互相帮助。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Shàng ge xīngqī, Tāngmǔ bìng le. Tā tóu téng, dùzi yě téng, liǎng tiān méi qù shàngkè. Xiǎoměi gěi tā mǎi lái le yào hé shuǐguǒ. Tā shuō: "Duō xiūxi, duō hē shuǐ, nǐ hěn kuài jiù huì hǎo de." Tāngmǔ chī le yào, shuì le shí'èr ge xiǎoshí. Dì èr tiān, tā juéde hǎo duō le. Tā gěi Xiǎoměi dǎ diànhuà: "Xièxie nǐ! Yīnwèi nǐ de bāngzhù, suǒyǐ wǒ hǎo de zhème kuài." Xiǎoměi xiào zhe shuō: "Bié kèqi! Péngyou jiù shì yào hùxiāng bāngzhù."

Last week Tom fell ill. His head hurt, his stomach too, and he missed class for two days. Xiaomei bought him medicine and fruit. She said: "Rest a lot, drink lots of water — you'll be better in no time." Tom took the medicine and slept twelve hours. The next day he felt much better. He phoned Xiaomei: "Thank you! It's thanks to your help that I got better so fast." Xiaomei said with a smile: "Don't mention it! Friends are there to help each other."

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How many days did Tom miss class?

readingQuestions.question: 小美给汤姆买来了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Xiaomei buy and bring Tom?

The book I bought is very interesting. → 我买____书很有意思。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: "The book that I bought" flips in Chinese: 我买的书 — I-bought-的 book. The whole description parks before the noun, clipped on with 的.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Description first, noun last (Z19)
helpMemoryTips.text: English: noun + that-clause. Chinese: clause + 的 + noun. 喝咖啡的人 = the person who's drinking coffee — read up to 的, then meet the noun.

helpMemoryTips.title: No who/which/that
helpMemoryTips.text: Chinese has no relative pronoun at all: the 的 does everything. 我认识的老师 — the teacher (whom) I know.

the students who are learning Chinese

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The 的-clause stretches: place, time and objects all ride along in front of the noun. Practice parsing from 的 backwards.

helpMemoryTips.title: Find the 的, find the noun
helpMemoryTips.text: In a long sentence, locate 的 + noun first, then read the description before it. 在北京工作的那个美国人 → that American / who works in Beijing.

quizzes.title: Speaking: describing people

subjects.display: 穿红衣服的那个人是谁？

Wǒ xǐhuan ài xiào de rén. — I like people who love to laugh.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Describe people aloud — feel the description stacking up BEFORE the person it describes.

helpMemoryTips.title: Build left, land right
helpMemoryTips.text: Say the description as one breath and land on the noun: 穿红衣服的//那个人. The noun is the finish line (Z19).

quizzes.title: 是…的 — spotlighting the details

subjects.display: It was yesterday that I came.

sentences.sentence: It was last year that they got to know each other. → 他们是____认识的。
sentences.english: It was last year that they got to know each other.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: For past events, 是…的 spotlights when/where/how: 我是昨天来的 — it was YESTERDAY that I came. The event is known; the detail is the news.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Known event, new detail (Z28)
helpMemoryTips.text: Use 是…的 when the happening is old news and you're asking or telling the circumstance: 你是怎么来的? (HOW did you come?) — not plain 了, which reports the event itself.

helpMemoryTips.title: The frame
helpMemoryTips.text: 是 + [spotlighted detail + verb] + 的: 她是在北京学的中文, 我们是坐飞机来的.

quizzes.title: Listening: 他是什么时候来的?
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Every answer in this dialogue is a 是…的 spotlight: when, from where, how, with whom. Catch each detail.

helpMemoryTips.title: 从…来 = come from
helpMemoryTips.text: 从 (from) is a coverb: 从加拿大来 — from-Canada come. Another scene-setter that stands before the verb (Z29).

quizzes.readingPassage:
小美："我们班有一个新同学，你见过他吗？"
汤姆："见过。他是上个月来的。"
小美："他是从哪儿来的？"
汤姆："他是从加拿大来的，是坐飞机来的。"
小美："他的中文说得怎么样？"
汤姆："说得非常好！他是在家跟妈妈学的——他妈妈是中国人。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒmen bān yǒu yí ge xīn tóngxué, nǐ jiàn guo tā ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Jiàn guo. Tā shì shàng ge yuè lái de."
Xiǎoměi: "Tā shì cóng nǎr lái de?"
Tāngmǔ: "Tā shì cóng Jiānádà lái de, shì zuò fēijī lái de."
Xiǎoměi: "Tā de Zhōngwén shuō de zěnmeyàng?"
Tāngmǔ: "Shuō de fēicháng hǎo! Tā shì zài jiā gēn māma xué de — tā māma shì Zhōngguó rén."

Xiaomei: "There's a new classmate in our class — have you met him?"
Tom: "I have. He came last month."
Xiaomei: "Where is he from?"
Tom: "He's from Canada — he came by plane."
Xiaomei: "How's his Chinese?"
Tom: "Excellent! He learned it at home with his mum — his mum is Chinese."

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 如果 A，B 就… — if A, then B. The 就 sits inside the second clause, right before its verb: 如果下雨，我们就不去.

helpMemoryTips.title: Another pair to keep (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 如果 opens the condition, 就 answers it. 就 is an adverb: it must stand before the verb, never before the subject — 就我们不去 ✗.

helpMemoryTips.title: No tense gymnastics
helpMemoryTips.text: English shifts tenses ("if it rains… we would…"); Chinese conditions stay bare: 如果…就 handles real and hypothetical alike (Z9).

helpMemoryTips.title: Three frames, one drawer
helpMemoryTips.text: 又便宜又好吃 cheap AND tasty · 天气越来越热 hotter and hotter · 越学越有意思 the more you study, the more interesting it gets.

sentences.sentence: I can't see it (too far away). (look-register) → 太远了，我看____见。

sentences.english: I can't see it (too far away). (look-register)

sentences.sentence: We can't buy it (too expensive → can't attain). (buy-起 = afford) → 太贵了，我们买____起。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Slide 得 or 不 between verb and landing to say whether the result is reachable: 听得懂 can understand, 听不懂 can't understand.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ The landing decides, 得/不 predicts (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: 看得完 can finish reading it, 看不完 can't possibly finish. This beats 能 for ability tied to a RESULT: 我听不懂 ≈ "it won't land in my ears".

helpMemoryTips.title: Questions pair both
helpMemoryTips.text: 你听得懂听不懂? or 你听得懂吗? — either asks "can you follow?"

quizzes.title: Reading: 我认识的人
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Four people, each introduced by a 的-clause. Parse each: find the 的, find the noun, then read the description before it.

helpMemoryTips.title: Chunk, don't crawl (Z8)
helpMemoryTips.text: 住在他楼上的|老爷爷 — split at the 的. Reading Chinese means grouping characters into words and clauses; the 的 is your best seam.

quizzes.readingPassage: 在北京，汤姆认识了很多有意思的人。住在他楼上的老爷爷每天早上在公园里打太极拳，他是三十年前从上海来的。在咖啡馆工作的那个女孩儿会说四种语言，她说得又快又好。教汤姆写汉字的王老师写的字漂亮得像画儿一样。汤姆觉得，认识的人越多，他的中文就越好，生活也越来越有意思。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Zài Běijīng, Tāngmǔ rènshi le hěn duō yǒuyìsi de rén. Zhù zài tā lóushàng de lǎo yéye měitiān zǎoshang zài gōngyuán li dǎ tàijíquán, tā shì sānshí nián qián cóng Shànghǎi lái de. Zài kāfēiguǎn gōngzuò de nà ge nǚháir huì shuō sì zhǒng yǔyán, tā shuō de yòu kuài yòu hǎo. Jiāo Tāngmǔ xiě Hànzì de Wáng lǎoshī xiě de zì piàoliang de xiàng huàr yíyàng. Tāngmǔ juéde, rènshi de rén yuè duō, tā de Zhōngwén jiù yuè hǎo, shēnghuó yě yuèláiyuè yǒuyìsi.

In Beijing, Tom has gotten to know many interesting people. The old grandpa who lives upstairs does tai chi in the park every morning — he came from Shanghai thirty years ago. The girl who works at the café speaks four languages, fast and well. Teacher Wang, who teaches Tom to write characters, writes characters as beautiful as paintings. Tom finds that the more people he knows, the better his Chinese gets — and life keeps getting more interesting.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Some "verbs" are secretly verb + object: 见面 = see-face, 帮忙 = help-busy. They split open to take 了, durations — and never take another object.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 见面他 ✗ — meet WITH: 跟他见面
helpMemoryTips.text: 面 already fills the object slot, so the person joins with 跟: 我跟他见面. Same family: 帮他的忙, 睡了一个好觉, 唱了三首歌.

quizzes.title: Weather & seasons

subjects.display: The weather today is really good!

sentences.sentence: The weather today is really good! → 今天____真好！
sentences.english: The weather today is really good!

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Weather verbs act alone: 下雨 it's raining ("falls rain"), 刮风 it's windy — no "it" needed. Seasons: 春夏秋冬.

helpMemoryTips.title: No dummy "it" (Z28)
helpMemoryTips.text: English props weather on "it"; Chinese just states the event: 下雨了 raining, 下雪了 snowing, 刮风了 wind's up. Subjectless and proud.

quizzes.title: Speaking: read in chunks, not characters

subjects.display: 我昨天买的那本书很有意思。

subjects.display: 住在楼上的爷爷每天打太极拳。

Tā shuō de huà wǒ dōu tīng de dǒng. — I can understand everything she says.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Chinese writes without spaces — fluent reading (and speaking) groups characters into words and phrases. Read each line as its chunks.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Chunk at 的 and the commas (Z8)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我昨天买的|那本书|很有意思 — three chunks, three breaths. Character-by-character reading kills both speed and tone.

quizzes.title: Listening: 天气预报
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A weather forecast for four cities. Listen for city + weather + temperature — and one 比-comparison.

helpMemoryTips.title: 度 = degrees, 零下 = below zero
helpMemoryTips.text: 二十八度 28°, 零下十度 −10°. The 比-line: 比今天热三度 — hotter than today BY three degrees (the amount follows the adjective, Z24).

quizzes.readingPassage: 大家好，现在播报明天的天气。北京明天是晴天，不刮风，白天二十八度，是个又暖和又舒服的日子。上海明天上午有小雨，下午雨就停了，二十五度。广州明天天气很热，三十四度，比今天热三度。哈尔滨的朋友要注意：明天下大雪，零下十度，出门的时候要多穿衣服。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Dàjiā hǎo, xiànzài bōbào míngtiān de tiānqì. Běijīng míngtiān shì qíngtiān, bù guā fēng, báitiān èrshíbā dù, shì ge yòu nuǎnhuo yòu shūfu de rìzi. Shànghǎi míngtiān shàngwǔ yǒu xiǎo yǔ, xiàwǔ yǔ jiù tíng le, èrshíwǔ dù. Guǎngzhōu míngtiān tiānqì hěn rè, sānshísì dù, bǐ jīntiān rè sān dù. Hā'ěrbīn de péngyou yào zhùyì: míngtiān xià dà xuě, língxià shí dù, chūmén de shíhou yào duō chuān yīfu.

Hello everyone, here is tomorrow's weather. Beijing: sunny, no wind, 28 degrees in the day — a warm, comfortable day. Shanghai: light rain in the morning, stopping by afternoon, 25 degrees. Guangzhou: very hot, 34 degrees — three degrees hotter than today. Friends in Harbin, take note: heavy snow tomorrow, minus ten — dress warmly when you go out.

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When does the rain in Shanghai stop?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear — 的-clauses, 是…的 spotlights and potential complements included.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Hear the clause seam
helpMemoryTips.text: In 我昨天买的书, the tiny 的 splits clause from noun. Miss it and the IME will offer you nonsense — the seam is the meaning (Z19).

quizzes.title: Reading: 北京的四季
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Four seasons, packed with this module's frames: 又…又, 越来越, 的-clauses and a closing 如果…就.

helpMemoryTips.title: 最 = the most
helpMemoryTips.text: 最热 hottest, 最漂亮 most beautiful, 最喜欢 favourite — 最 simply fronts the adjective. No "-est" forms to build.

quizzes.readingPassage: 北京的四季很不一样。春天暖和，可是常常刮风。夏天又热又长，最热的时候有三十八度，白天出门的人都走得很快，因为大家都想快点儿回到凉快的家里。秋天是北京最漂亮的季节：天很蓝，路两边的树越来越黄，来公园拍照片的人也越来越多。冬天很冷，有时候下大雪。下雪的时候，孩子们玩得最高兴。汤姆最喜欢的季节是秋天。他说："如果你秋天来北京，就会爱上这个城市。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Běijīng de sìjì hěn bù yíyàng. Chūntiān nuǎnhuo, kěshì chángcháng guā fēng. Xiàtiān yòu rè yòu cháng, zuì rè de shíhou yǒu sānshíbā dù, báitiān chūmén de rén dōu zǒu de hěn kuài, yīnwèi dàjiā dōu xiǎng kuài diǎnr huí dào liángkuai de jiā li. Qiūtiān shì Běijīng zuì piàoliang de jìjié: tiān hěn lán, lù liǎngbiān de shù yuèláiyuè huáng, lái gōngyuán pāi zhàopiàn de rén yě yuèláiyuè duō. Dōngtiān hěn lěng, yǒushíhou xià dà xuě. Xià xuě de shíhou, háizimen wán de zuì gāoxìng. Tāngmǔ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié shì qiūtiān. Tā shuō: "Rúguǒ nǐ qiūtiān lái Běijīng, jiù huì àishàng zhè ge chéngshì."

Beijing's four seasons are very different. Spring is warm but often windy. Summer is hot and long — at its hottest it reaches 38 degrees, and people out in the daytime walk fast, because everyone wants to get back to a cool home. Autumn is Beijing's most beautiful season: the sky is blue, the trees along the roads turn more and more yellow, and more and more people come to the parks to take photos. Winter is cold, sometimes with heavy snow. When it snows, the children have the best time. Tom's favourite season is autumn. He says: "If you come to Beijing in autumn, you'll fall in love with this city."

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Which is Beijing's most beautiful season?

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How hot does it get at the height of summer?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: To say what you DID to something, grab it first: 我把门关上了 — I took the door and shut it. 把 + object + verb + landing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Grab it, then do it (Z22)
helpMemoryTips.text: S + 把 + object + verb + RESULT. The verb can't stand bare: 把门关 ✗ — it needs a landing (关上, 吃完, 放在…). 把 fronts the object so the action's effect takes the spotlight.

helpMemoryTips.title: When to reach for 把
helpMemoryTips.text: Known, specific object + what happened to it → 把. Telling someone what to do with things (put, move, finish, close) practically demands it.

quizzes.title: 把 + where it lands: 在 / 到 / 给

subjects.display: Put the book on the table. (lands ON)
He drove me to the airport. (lands AT)
Hand the homework to the teacher. (lands WITH person)
Please put the phone in the bag.
I sent the photo to my mum. (发 = send)
Translate this sentence into English. (翻译成 = translate-into)

sentences.sentence: Hand the homework to the teacher. (lands WITH person) → 把作业交____老师。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The landing after a 把-verb often tells WHERE or TO WHOM: 放在桌子上 put ON the table, 送到机场 deliver TO the airport, 交给老师 hand TO the teacher.

helpMemoryTips.title: V + 在/到/给 + place/person (Z22)
helpMemoryTips.text: 把 X 放**在** place / 送**到** destination / 交**给** person. These three endings cover most of what you ever do with objects.

quizzes.title: Speaking: instructions with 把

subjects.english: Bǎ zhuōzi bān dào kètīng. — Move the table into the living room.
Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng. — Please shut the door.
Bǎ yīfu fàng zài chuáng shàng ba. — Put the clothes on the bed.
Bié bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā li! — Don't leave the keys at home!
Bǎ zhè bēi chá ná gěi nǎinai. — Take this cup of tea to grandma.
Bǎ nǐ de xíngli fàng zài zhèr. — Put your luggage here.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Give instructions aloud — moving-day orders are pure 把 territory: grab the thing, say where it goes.

helpMemoryTips.title: Rhythm: 把-X | V-landing
helpMemoryTips.text: Chunk each order in two: 把桌子 | 搬到客厅. The pause after the object keeps long instructions clear (Z22).

subjects.display: The cake was eaten by my little brother.
My phone was taken away by the teacher.
The window was broken by the wind. (打破 = break)
He was criticized by the boss. (批评 = criticize)
The last piece of duck got eaten by Tom.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 被 flips the sentence: 蛋糕被弟弟吃了 — the cake got eaten by little brother. Classic 被 carries a whiff of misfortune.

helpMemoryTips.title: Victim + 被 + (culprit) + verb + landing (Z23)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我的自行车被(人)偷了 — my bike got stolen. The culprit is optional; the landing (了, 走, 完…) is not.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't translate every English passive with 被
helpMemoryTips.text: "The problem was solved" is NOT 被: say 问题解决了 (next quiz). 被 fits mishaps and formal reports — overusing it is textbook foreign accent.

quizzes.title: The notional passive: 问题解决了

subjects.display: The clothes are washed. (wash-clean: 洗干净)

sentences.sentence: The problem is solved. (no 被!) → 问题____了。
The tickets are bought. → 票____了。
The letter is written. (write-finish) → 信____了。
The clothes are washed. (wash-clean: 洗干净) → 衣服____了。
sentences.english: The clothes are washed. (wash-clean: 洗干净)

sentences.sentence: This book sold out. (sell-finish) → 这本书____了。
sentences.hint: zhè běn shū mài wán le

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Chinese's favourite passive has no marker at all: topic first, verb after — 问题解决了 the problem (got) solved, 饭做好了 dinner's ready.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Topic + verb, no 被 (Z23/Z28)
helpMemoryTips.text: When no culprit matters and nothing bad happened, drop the passive machinery: 票买好了 tickets are bought, 信写完了 the letter's written. This is the natural voice of Chinese.

quizzes.title: Listening: 谁把蛋糕吃了?
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A missing-cake mystery, told in 把 and 被. (From now on the info button is English-only — your pinyin training wheels are off.)

helpMemoryTips.title: 把 accuses, 被 defends
helpMemoryTips.text: 谁把蛋糕吃了? points at a doer; 蛋糕没被人吃 clears everyone. The same event, grabbed from both ends (Z22/Z23).

quizzes.readingPassage:
晚上，小美回到家，打开冰箱，发现她的生日蛋糕不见了。
小美："谁把我的蛋糕吃了？！"

爸爸："我也没吃。你去问问你妈妈。"

In the evening, Xiaomei comes home, opens the fridge, and finds her birthday cake gone.
Xiaomei: "Who ate my cake?!"
Little brother: "Not me! I was playing football all afternoon."
Dad: "I didn't eat it either. Go ask your mum."
Mum laughs: "Nobody ate the cake — I moved it upstairs, because tonight we're giving you a surprise. Happy birthday!"

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 让 (and casual 叫) hand an action to someone else: 妈妈让我学中文 — mum has/lets me study Chinese. Negate in front: 不让.

helpMemoryTips.title: A + 让 + B + verb
helpMemoryTips.text: The second verb belongs to B: 老板让我们加班 the boss makes us work late; 别让我等 don't make me wait. English "make/let/have someone do" collapses into 让.
