sentences.english: He speaks as well as the teacher. (一样 + 好)

sentences.sentence: Chinese is even more interesting than I thought. (比我想的) → 中文比我想的____有意思。
sentences.hint: Zhōngwén bǐ wǒ xiǎng de gèng yǒuyìsi
sentences.english: Chinese is even more interesting than I thought. (比我想的)
sentences.referenceExample: 中文比我想的**更**有意思。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Beyond plain 比: 更 even more, 最 the most, 跟…一样 the same as, 没有…那么 not as … as.

helpMemoryTips.title: Four tools, four jobs (Z24)
helpMemoryTips.text: A 比 B 高 taller · A 比 B **更**高 even taller (B is tall too!) · A **最**高 tallest · A **跟** B **一样**高 equally tall · A **没有** B **那么**高 not as tall.

quizzes.title: Reading: 搬家
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Moving day: instructions with 把, one 被 for flavour, and comparisons between old home and new.

helpMemoryTips.title: 离 = distance from (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 新家离学校更近 — 离 measures the gap between two places: A 离 B 近/远. It's a coverb: it stands before what it relates to.

quizzes.readingPassage:
这个周末汤姆搬家了。新家比旧家大得多，离学校也更近。
小美和几个朋友都来帮忙。汤姆让大家先把大东西搬上车：床、桌子、椅子，还有那个最重的书柜。
"把书柜放在哪儿？"小美问。
"放在窗户旁边吧，"汤姆说，"把书都放到书柜里，把衣服放在床上，我等一下自己收拾。"
搬完家，大家都累了。汤姆把大家的水杯拿来，说："今天真是太感谢你们了！晚上我请大家吃饭——菜已经被我订好了！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
This weekend Tom moved house. The new place is much bigger than the old one, and closer to school too.
Xiaomei and a few friends came to help. Tom had everyone move the big things onto the truck first: the bed, the table, the chairs, and that heaviest of bookcases.
"Where do we put the bookcase?" Xiaomei asked.
"Next to the window," said Tom. "Put the books in the bookcase and the clothes on the bed — I'll sort them out myself later."
When the move was done, everyone was exhausted. Tom brought everyone's water and said: "Thank you all so much for today! Dinner's on me tonight — the food is already ordered!"

readingQuestions.question: 新家怎么样？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What is the new home like?

readingQuestions.question: 晚上谁请大家吃饭？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who treats everyone to dinner in the evening?

quizzes.title: Abstract directions: 起来 / 下去 / 出来

subjects.display: Keep studying (persist onward) — don't give up.
Could you tell (by listening) that he's British?
The weather is starting to get hot.

sentences.sentence: I remembered! (the thought came up) → 我想____了！
Keep studying (persist onward) — don't give up. → 坚持____，别放弃。
sentences.english: Keep studying (persist onward) — don't give up.

sentences.sentence: She suddenly burst out laughing. → 她忽然笑了____。
Could you tell (by listening) that he's British? → 你听____他是英国人吗？
sentences.hint: nǐ tīng chūlái tā shì Yīngguó rén ma
sentences.english: Could you tell (by listening) that he's British?
sentences.referenceExample: 你听**出来**他是英国人吗？

sentences.sentence: Please continue speaking. (speak onward) → 请说____。
The weather is starting to get hot. → 天气热____了。
sentences.english: The weather is starting to get hot.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Directional complements go abstract: 想起来 recall (thought comes UP), 坚持下去 keep going (persist DOWNWARD/onward), 听出来 tell by ear (hear it OUT).

helpMemoryTips.title: Directions become metaphors (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: 起来 = starting/surfacing (笑起来 burst out laughing, 想起来 it comes back to me). 下去 = continuing (说下去 go on). 出来 = emerging/identifying (看出来 spot it).

quizzes.title: Speaking: question intonation OVER tones

subjects.english: Nǐ qù ma? — Are you going? (去 still falls!)
Nǐ shì shéi? — Who are you? (statement melody)
Nǐ bǎ yàoshi fàng zài nǎr le? — Where did you put the keys?
Zhè ge duōshao qián? — How much is this? (calm, no English rise)
Nǐ tīng de dǒng tīng bu dǒng? — Can you follow or not?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A Chinese question rises as a whole — but every syllable keeps its own tone. Don't let English question-melody bend the words.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ The sentence rises, the tones survive (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: In 你去吗? the overall pitch floats up, but 去 still FALLS (4th tone) inside that float. English speakers turn 去 into a rise — and say a different word.

quizzes.title: Work & office

subjects.display: The manager has us in a meeting every Monday.

sentences.sentence: The manager has us in a meeting every Monday. → 经理____我们每星期一开会。
sentences.hint: jīnglǐ ràng wǒmen měi xīngqīyī kāihuì
sentences.english: The manager has us in a meeting every Monday.
sentences.referenceExample: 经理**让**我们每星期一开会。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The vocabulary of jobs and offices — where 把-instructions and polite 让-requests live all day.

helpMemoryTips.title: 班 = your shift
helpMemoryTips.text: 上班 go on shift (start work), 下班 come off shift, 加班 add shift (overtime) — one noun, three daily verbs.

quizzes.title: Listening: 面试
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Tom's job interview — 把…翻译成, a potential complement, and polite workplace Chinese.

helpMemoryTips.title: 您 = polite you
helpMemoryTips.text: 您 nín is 你 with a heart (心) underneath — the respectful "you" for bosses, elders and customers. 谢谢您!

quizzes.readingPassage:
汤姆想找一份兼职工作，今天他去一家翻译公司面试。
经理："你为什么想来我们公司工作？"
汤姆："因为我喜欢语言。我会说英文和法文，中文也说得越来越好。"
经理："你能把这段中文翻译成英文吗？"
汤姆看了看，把那段话翻译了出来。
经理很满意："翻译得不错！下星期一你能来上班吗？"
汤姆高兴地说："能！谢谢您给我这个机会。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Tom wants a part-time job, and today he has an interview at a translation company.
Manager: "Why do you want to work at our company?"
Tom: "Because I love languages. I speak English and French, and my Chinese keeps getting better."
Manager: "Can you translate this Chinese passage into English?"
Tom looks it over and translates the passage.
The manager is pleased: "Nicely translated! Can you start next Monday?"
Tom says happily: "I can! Thank you for giving me this opportunity."

readingQuestions.question: 经理让汤姆做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does the manager have Tom do?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆什么时候开始上班？

quizzes.title: Dictation: 把-sentences

subjects.english: I put the book on the table.

subjects.display: 我的手机被老师拿走了。
subjects.english: My phone was taken by the teacher.
Hand the homework to the teacher.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear — the 把 fronts the object, so hold the whole sentence in your ear before typing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 把 vs 被 — one syllable apart
helpMemoryTips.text: bǎ (3rd tone) grabs, bèi (4th tone) suffers. In fast speech only the tone separates who did it from who got it done to (Z22/Z23).

quizzes.title: Reading: 中国的快递
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A slice of modern China — full of this module's grammar: 把, 被, comparisons and a 让 at the end.

helpMemoryTips.title: 被 without a culprit
helpMemoryTips.text: 能被送到家门口 / 能被再次使用 — formal-neutral 被 with no agent is fine in written style. Speech would just say 送到家门口 (Z23).

quizzes.readingPassage:
在中国生活了一年以后，汤姆觉得最方便的就是快递。你在手机上买的东西，第二天就能被送到家门口。快递员每天把成千上万个包裹送到城市的每一个角落，比很多国家的快递快得多，也便宜得多。
上个星期，汤姆把一本书寄给在上海的朋友。他早上把书交给快递员，朋友第二天中午就收到了。朋友给他发消息："收到了！这也太快了吧！"
不过快递也带来了新问题：人们买得越来越多，包装垃圾也越来越多。现在很多公司开始让顾客把纸箱留给快递员，这样纸箱就能被再次使用。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
After a year of living in China, Tom thinks the most convenient thing of all is the express delivery system. Something you buy on your phone can be delivered to your door the next day. Couriers deliver tens of thousands of parcels to every corner of the city every day — much faster and much cheaper than in many countries.
Last week, Tom mailed a book to a friend in Shanghai. He handed the book to the courier in the morning, and his friend received it the next day at noon. The friend messaged him: "Got it! That's just too fast!"
But delivery brings new problems too: people buy more and more, and packaging waste keeps growing. Many companies now have customers leave the boxes with the courier, so the boxes can be used again.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆觉得在中国生活最方便的是什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom find most convenient about life in China?

readingQuestions.question: 朋友什么时候收到了书？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When did the friend receive the book?

readingQuestions.question: 快递带来了什么新问题？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What new problem does delivery bring?

quizzes.title: 着 — states that stay on

subjects.display: She is wearing a red coat.
A photo hangs on the wall.
The lights are on. (开 works for lights too)

sentences.sentence: The door is (standing) open. → 门开____。
She is wearing a red coat. → 她穿____红大衣。
sentences.english: She is wearing a red coat.

sentences.sentence: A photo hangs on the wall. → 墙上挂____一张照片。
sentences.hint: qiáng shàng guà zhe yì zhāng zhàopiàn
sentences.english: A photo hangs on the wall.

sentences.sentence: He said it smiling. (smile-着 say) → 他笑____说。
We sat chatting. (sit-着 chat) → 我们坐____聊天。
The lights are on. (开 works for lights too) → 灯开____。
sentences.english: The lights are on. (开 works for lights too)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 着 zhe freezes an action into a state: 门开着 the door stands open, 她穿着红衣服 she's wearing red. Also: V1着 V2 — doing B while A-ing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 着 = the pause button (Z16)
helpMemoryTips.text: 开 is opening; 开着 is standing open. 了 stamps the change, 着 holds the resulting state. 墙上挂着一张照片 — a photo hangs on the wall.

helpMemoryTips.title: V着 + V = while
helpMemoryTips.text: 她笑着说 she said, smiling; 我们坐着聊天 we sat chatting. The 着-verb paints the backdrop of the main verb.

quizzes.title: 就 vs 才 — sooner vs later

subjects.display: He didn't come UNTIL ten (late — and no 了!).
I understood after listening once (that easily).
She only fell asleep at 2 a.m. (so late).
The food came right after we sat down. (that quickly)
I only now understand this. (现在才)

sentences.sentence: He came at eight ALREADY (early). → 他八点____来了。
sentences.hint: tā bā diǎn jiù lái le

sentences.sentence: He didn't come UNTIL ten (late — and no 了!). → 他十点____来。
sentences.english: He didn't come UNTIL ten (late — and no 了!).

sentences.sentence: I understood after listening once (that easily). → 我听了一遍____懂了。
sentences.hint: wǒ tīng le yí biàn jiù dǒng le
sentences.english: I understood after listening once (that easily).

sentences.sentence: She only fell asleep at 2 a.m. (so late). → 她两点____睡着。
sentences.english: She only fell asleep at 2 a.m. (so late).

sentences.sentence: The food came right after we sat down. (that quickly) → 我们一坐下，菜____来了。
sentences.hint: wǒmen yí zuò xià, cài jiù lái le
sentences.english: The food came right after we sat down. (that quickly)

sentences.sentence: I only now understand this. (现在才) → 我现在____明白。
sentences.english: I only now understand this. (现在才)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The attitude twins: 八点就来了 — came at eight (early!); 八点才来 — didn't come UNTIL eight (finally!). Same clock, opposite feelings.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 就 = sooner than you think, 才 = later than you'd like (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 就 says "that fast/easy/soon"; 才 says "only then, not before". Note: 才 blocks 了 — 他十点才来(了✗).

quizzes.title: 再 vs 又 — the two "agains"

subjects.display: Please say it one more time. (future repeat)
Let's eat first and talk later. (先…再)
She watched the film again (and had seen it before).

sentences.sentence: He was late again (it happened). → 他____迟到了。
Please say it one more time. (future repeat) → 请____说一遍。
sentences.english: Please say it one more time. (future repeat)

sentences.sentence: It rained again yesterday. → 昨天____下雨了。
Come again tomorrow. → 明天____来吧。
Let's eat first and talk later. (先…再) → 先吃饭，____说。
sentences.english: Let's eat first and talk later. (先…再)

sentences.sentence: She watched the film again (and had seen it before). → 她____看了一遍那个电影。
sentences.hint: tā yòu kàn le yí biàn nà ge diànyǐng
sentences.english: She watched the film again (and had seen it before).
sentences.referenceExample: 她**又**看了一遍那个电影。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Both mean "again", split by time: 又 for repeats that already happened (他又来了), 再 for repeats still to come (明天再来).

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 又 looks back, 再 looks forward (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 又迟到了 — late AGAIN (it happened). 再说一遍 — say it again (please, in the future). 再见 = see you again — future, hence 再.

quizzes.title: Speaking: attitude particles 吧 / 呢 / 啊

subjects.english: Nǐ shì xuésheng ba? — You're a student, right?
Wǒ de yàoshi ne? — And where are my keys?
Zhè ge cài zhēn hǎochī a! — This dish is SO good!
Xiūxi yíxià ba. — Take a break, why don't you.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: One syllable of attitude: 吧 suggests or guesses, 呢 muses "and…?", 啊 warms and exclaims. Say them lightly — they ride the sentence's tail.

helpMemoryTips.title: The tail carries the tone of voice
helpMemoryTips.text: 走吧 let's go (suggestion) · 你是学生吧? you're a student, right? (guess) · 我的书呢? and where's my book? · 真好啊! how nice! All neutral-toned, all attitude.

quizzes.title: The 都 / 也 / 还 slots

subjects.display: I have read all of these books. (front the books!)
He is still working. (still at it)
I want another cup of coffee. (in addition: 还要)

sentences.sentence: We are all going. → 我们____去。
I have read all of these books. (front the books!) → 这些书我____看过。
sentences.hint: zhèxiē shū wǒ dōu kàn guo
sentences.english: I have read all of these books. (front the books!)

sentences.sentence: She also likes Chinese food. → 她____喜欢中国菜。
He is still working. (still at it) → 他____在工作。
sentences.english: He is still working. (still at it)

sentences.sentence: I want another cup of coffee. (in addition: 还要) → 我____要一杯咖啡。
sentences.hint: wǒ hái yào yì bēi kāfēi
sentences.english: I want another cup of coffee. (in addition: 还要)

sentences.sentence: Everyone understood. (大家 + all) → 大家____听懂了。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 都 all, 也 also, 还 still/in addition — small adverbs with a fixed home: after the subject, before the verb. 都 sums up what stands BEFORE it.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 都 points backward (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我们都去 — ALL of us go: 都 covers the crowd to its LEFT. "I read all the books" = 这些书我都看过 — front the books so 都 can see them.

helpMemoryTips.title: Order in the slot: 也 > 都 > 还
helpMemoryTips.text: Stacked, they keep this order: 我们也都还在等 — also-all-still waiting. Each stays before the verb, never after.

quizzes.title: Listening: 等人
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: One little story, all the little adverbs: 就 (early), 才 (finally), 又 (again!), 还 (still), plus a 着 and a 吧.

helpMemoryTips.title: 就要…了 = about to
helpMemoryTips.text: 电影就要开始了 — on the very edge of starting. 就 + 要 + verb + 了 is the "any second now" frame (Z27).

quizzes.readingPassage:
星期六下午两点，汤姆和小美约好在电影院门口见面，电影两点半开始。
汤姆一点半就到了，站着等小美。两点过了，小美还没来。他给小美发消息："你到哪儿了？电影就要开始了！"
两点二十五，小美才跑来，笑着说："对不起对不起！我又坐错车了！"
汤姆说："你上次也坐错了！快走吧，再不进去，电影就开始了！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Saturday afternoon at two, Tom and Xiaomei have agreed to meet at the cinema entrance; the film starts at half past two.
Tom arrives at half past one already and stands there waiting. Two o'clock passes — still no Xiaomei. He messages her: "Where are you? The film is about to start!"
At 2:25 Xiaomei finally comes running, saying with a laugh: "Sorry, sorry! I took the wrong bus again!"
Tom says: "You took the wrong one last time too! Quick — if we don't go in now, the film will start!"

readingQuestions.question: 小美是第几次坐错车？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Is this the first time Xiaomei took the wrong bus?

quizzes.title: Strong pairs: 不但…而且 / 只要…就 / 只有…才

subjects.display: He not only speaks Chinese, but also writes characters.
As long as you practise every day, you'll (then) improve.
Only by practising can you (only then) improve.
This dish is not only cheap but also delicious.
As long as it doesn't rain, we'll (then) go.
Only the people who finished the homework can (only then) watch TV.

sentences.sentence: He not only speaks Chinese, but also writes characters. → 他____会说中文，而且会写汉字。
sentences.hint: tā búdàn huì shuō Zhōngwén, érqiě huì xiě Hànzì
sentences.english: He not only speaks Chinese, but also writes characters.
sentences.referenceExample: 他**不但**会说中文，而且会写汉字。

sentences.sentence: As long as you practise every day, you'll (then) improve. → 只要你每天练习，____会进步。
sentences.hint: zhǐyào nǐ měitiān liànxí, jiù huì jìnbù
sentences.english: As long as you practise every day, you'll (then) improve.
sentences.referenceExample: 只要你每天练习，**就**会进步。

sentences.sentence: Only by practising can you (only then) improve. → 只有多练习，____会进步。
sentences.hint: zhǐyǒu duō liànxí, cái huì jìnbù
sentences.english: Only by practising can you (only then) improve.

sentences.sentence: This dish is not only cheap but also delicious. → 这个菜不但便宜，____很好吃。
sentences.hint: zhè ge cài búdàn piányi, érqiě hěn hǎochī
sentences.english: This dish is not only cheap but also delicious.
sentences.referenceExample: 这个菜不但便宜，**而且**很好吃。

sentences.sentence: As long as it doesn't rain, we'll (then) go. → ____不下雨，我们就去。
sentences.hint: zhǐyào bú xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù qù
sentences.english: As long as it doesn't rain, we'll (then) go.

sentences.sentence: Only the people who finished the homework can (only then) watch TV. → ____写完作业，才能看电视。
sentences.hint: zhǐyǒu xiě wán zuòyè, cái néng kàn diànshì
sentences.english: Only the people who finished the homework can (only then) watch TV.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Three heavyweight pairs: 不但 A 而且 B (not only… but also), 只要 A 就 B (as long as → enough), 只有 A 才 B (only if → necessary).

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 只要…就 is generous, 只有…才 is strict (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 只要练习，就会进步 — ANY practice brings progress (sufficient). 只有练习，才会进步 — NOTHING BUT practice brings it (necessary). The closer (就 vs 才) matches the opener.

quizzes.title: Big text: 了 / 过 / 着 — the aspect story
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: One Saturday, ten gaps, three particles. For each: completed and counted → 了; life experience → 过; held state or backdrop → 着.

helpMemoryTips.title: The three stamps side by side (Z14/Z15/Z16)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了 = ✓ done · 过 = passport-stamped experience · 着 = pause button. If the sentence counts something (一杯, 二十分钟), 了. If it says "ever/never", 过. If something just hangs there, 着.

quizzes.readingPassage:
星期六早上，汤姆睡到九点。窗户开着，外面下着小雨。
他喝了一杯咖啡，然后坐着看书。这本书他以前看过一遍，可是越看越喜欢。
中午，小美来电话："你吃饭了吗？我知道一家新饭馆，我还没去过，一起去吧！"
饭馆里人很多。他们等了二十分钟才坐下。墙上挂着很多老照片，菜也很好吃。汤姆笑着说："下个星期我们再来吧！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation: Saturday morning Tom sleeps till nine. The window stands open; outside a light rain is falling. He drinks a cup of coffee, then sits reading. He's read this book once before, but likes it more with every page. At noon Xiaomei calls: "Have you eaten? I know a new restaurant — I haven't been yet. Let's go together!" The restaurant is packed. They wait twenty minutes before getting a table. Old photos hang on the walls, and the food is great. Tom says with a smile: "Let's come again next week!"

quizzes.title: Reading: 一次约会
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A first date told through the module's lens: 就 vs 才, 着-states, 不但…而且, 只有…才 — attitude in every line.

helpMemoryTips.title: 呢 keeps it warm
helpMemoryTips.text: The closing 我们还要再见面呢! carries a happy glow — 呢 softens a statement into shared excitement.

quizzes.readingPassage:
小美的姐姐上个月认识了一个男孩子，两个人都喜欢爬山，很快就熟了。
第一次约会，男孩子七点就到了饭馆门口，站着等她。姐姐七点半才到，因为路上堵车堵得厉害。她远远地看见他手里拿着一束花，心里就不紧张了。
吃饭的时候，两个人聊得很开心。他不但会做菜，而且也喜欢看书。姐姐回家以后对小美说："只有跟他聊天的时候，我才觉得时间过得这么快。我们下星期还要再见面呢！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Last month Xiaomei's older sister met a boy; they both love hiking and quickly hit it off.
For the first date, the boy arrived at the restaurant at seven already and stood waiting. The sister didn't arrive until half past — the traffic jam was terrible. From a distance she saw the bouquet in his hand, and her nerves melted away.
Over dinner the two talked happily. He not only cooks, but loves books too. Back home, the sister told Xiaomei: "Only when I'm talking with him does time pass this fast. We're meeting again next week!"

readingQuestions.question: 男孩子几点到的？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What time did the boy arrive?

quizzes.title: Concession: 即使…也 / 无论…都

subjects.display: Even if it rains, I will still go.
No matter how busy, you must always eat.

No matter where he goes, he always takes that book.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Bulletproof statements: 即使 A，也 B (even if A, still B), 无论 A，都 B (no matter A, always B).

helpMemoryTips.title: 也/都 close the pair (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 即使 pairs with 也; 无论 pairs with 都 — and 无论 wants an open question after it (谁/什么/多 or A不A): 无论多忙，都要吃饭.

quizzes.title: Speaking: connected speech at pace

subjects.english: Tā xiào zhe shuō: "Wǒmen zǒu ba!" — She said, smiling: "Let's go!"

subjects.english: Zhǐyào nǐ lái, wǒmen jiù hěn gāoxìng. — As long as you come, we'll be happy.

subjects.display: 他不但会做菜，而且做得非常好吃。
subjects.english: Tā búdàn huì zuò cài, érqiě zuò de fēicháng hǎochī. — He not only cooks — he cooks wonderfully.
Wúlùn duō wǎn, wǒ dōu děng nǐ. — However late, I'll wait for you.

subjects.english: Diànyǐng jiù yào kāishǐ le, kuài diǎnr a! — The film's about to start, hurry!

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Full sentences at natural speed: keep the particles light, the tones intact, and breathe at the commas.

helpMemoryTips.title: Light ≠ lost (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了, 着, 吧, 呢 go quiet and quick — but never vanish. Aim for "small but there": native rhythm keeps every syllable's slot.

quizzes.title: Feelings & opinions

subjects.display: In my view / opinion (looking at it my way)

sentences.sentence: I am interested in history. → 我____历史感兴趣。
In my view / opinion (looking at it my way) → ____
sentences.english: In my view / opinion (looking at it my way)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Words for the inner weather — and the frames that carry opinions: 我觉得… I feel/think, 对…感兴趣 interested in.

helpMemoryTips.title: 对 X 感兴趣
helpMemoryTips.text: Interest aims with 对: 我对历史感兴趣 — toward history I feel interest. Another coverb setting the scene before the verb (Z29).

quizzes.title: Listening: 播客 — 好习惯
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A podcast on habits — listen for 只要…就 vs 只有…才 doing real argumentative work, plus 着, 即使…也 and 无论…都.

helpMemoryTips.title: 听起来 = it sounds…
helpMemoryTips.text: 听起来很简单 — "hearing-wise it comes out simple". The abstract 起来 turns any verb into an impression: 看起来, 说起来 (Z21).

quizzes.readingPassage:
大家好，欢迎收听我们的播客。今天聊一个话题：好习惯是怎么来的？
很多人觉得，只要下定决心，就能改变自己。可是研究发现，只有把新习惯变得很小、很容易，才能坚持下去。比如，你想每天看书，就先从每天看一页开始。即使那天再忙，一页书也看得完。
还有一个方法：把新习惯放在老习惯后面。每天喝着咖啡的时候背五个生词——咖啡喝完了，生词也背完了。听起来很简单吧？无论你想养成什么习惯，都可以试试这个办法。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Hello everyone, welcome to our podcast. Today's topic: where do good habits come from?
Many people think that as long as you're determined, you can change yourself. But research finds that only by making a new habit small and easy can you keep it going. Say you want to read every day — start with one page a day. Even on your busiest day, one page is doable.
Another method: attach the new habit to an old one. Memorize five new words while drinking your daily coffee — when the coffee's finished, so are the words. Sounds simple, right? Whatever habit you want to build, give this method a try.

readingQuestions.question: 研究发现，怎样才能坚持新习惯？
options: 把习惯变得很小、很容易
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: According to research, how can you keep a new habit going?

readingQuestions.question: 想每天看书，应该从什么开始？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: To read daily, what should you start with?

readingQuestions.question: 喝咖啡的时候可以做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What can you do while drinking coffee?

quizzes.title: Dictation: attitude lines

subjects.english: Please say it one more time.
Let's go, the film is about to start!

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear — the meaning hides in the little words: 就, 才, 又, 再, 着, 吧.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ The adverbs are the message (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 他八点就来了 vs 他八点才来 — one small word flips early to late. If you're unsure what you heard, replay for the adverb, not the nouns.

quizzes.title: Reading: 手机与生活
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Modern China through this module's grammar: 着-states everywhere, 一边…一边, 只有…才, and a 谁…谁 pattern worth stealing.

helpMemoryTips.title: 谁…谁… = whoever
helpMemoryTips.text: 谁先拿手机，谁就请客 — whoever grabs the phone first, THAT person treats. The question word doubles as "whoever" (Z28).

quizzes.readingPassage:
在中国，手机几乎就是生活本身。人们用手机买东西、点外卖、坐地铁、看病挂号。汤姆刚来的时候还带着钱包，现在他出门只带手机——钱包在家里放着，已经放了半年了。
手机让生活变得方便，可是也带来了新问题。在地铁里，几乎每个人都低着头看手机；朋友们坐在一起吃饭，也常常是一边吃着饭，一边看着手机。
小美说："我们只有把手机放下，才能真正地在一起。"所以他们约好：吃饭的时候，谁先拿手机，谁就请客。这个办法听起来简单，可是很有用——即使是最爱看手机的朋友，也坚持下来了。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
In China, the phone practically IS daily life. People use it to shop, order food, ride the metro, register at the hospital. When Tom first arrived he still carried a wallet; now he leaves home with only his phone — the wallet has been sitting at home for half a year.
Phones make life convenient, but they bring new problems. On the metro, almost everyone rides with head bowed over a screen; friends sitting down to dinner often eat with one eye on their phones.
Xiaomei says: "Only by putting the phones down can we truly be together." So they made a deal: at dinner, whoever reaches for their phone first pays the bill. It sounds simple, but it works — even the most phone-addicted friend has stuck to it.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆现在出门带什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom take when he goes out now?

readingQuestions.question: 朋友们约好了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What deal did the friends make?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: HSK 5 lives on pairs that translate identically but behave differently: one takes an object, the other splits; one is an adjective too, the other only an adverb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Test the grammar, not the gloss
helpMemoryTips.text: 帮助 + person (帮助我); 帮忙 splits and takes none (帮我一个忙). 突然 can be an adjective (很突然); 忽然 only ever an adverb. The dictionary meaning is the same — the syntax isn't.

helpMemoryTips.title: More pairs on this shelf
helpMemoryTips.text: 常常 (often, habits) vs 往往 (tends to, patterns + conditions); 一定 (must/surely) vs 肯定 (certainly, can be a verb: 我肯定…).

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Three ways to make something happen to someone: colloquial 让, formal 使, and 令 for triggered emotions (令人吃惊 — astonishing).

helpMemoryTips.title: Register picks the causative
helpMemoryTips.text: Speech: 让 (这让我很高兴). Writing: 使 (这使我们的工作更容易). Fixed emotional frames: 令人 + feeling (令人失望, 令人感动).

quizzes.title: Speaking: presenting an opinion

subjects.display: 在我看来，这个问题并不简单。

Lìngwài, zhè yě shì yí ge jīhuì. — Besides, this is also an opportunity.

subjects.english: Dāngrán, měi ge rén de qíngkuàng bù yíyàng. — Of course, everyone's situation differs.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The skeleton of a spoken argument: state, support, concede, conclude — in connected, natural Mandarin.

helpMemoryTips.title: Signpost, then speak
helpMemoryTips.text: 在我看来 / 首先 / 另外 / 总的来说 — plant a signpost at each turn. Chinese listeners navigate arguments by these markers (Z30).

quizzes.title: 对 / 对于 / 关于 / 由于

subjects.display: I'm very interested in Chinese history. (aim: 对)

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The formal coverb set: 对/对于 toward (attitude), 关于 about (topic), 由于 owing to (cause). They frame the sentence before its verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Aim, topic, cause (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 对(于) aims an attitude at something; 关于 labels the topic (often fronted or in titles); 由于 gives the formal cause — and pairs happily with 因此.

quizzes.title: Listening: 讲座 — 城市化
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A university-style lecture: the formal register in action — 使, 由于, 对于, 关于, 令人, 既…也.

helpMemoryTips.title: 既…也 = both…and (formal)
helpMemoryTips.text: 既带来了机会，也带来了挑战 — the written cousin of 又…又, joining two verb phrases in balanced style (Z30).

quizzes.readingPassage:
各位同学，下午好。今天我们谈谈城市化。
过去四十年，中国经历了世界上规模最大的城市化：几亿人从农村搬进了城市。城市化使经济快速发展，也使几亿人的生活水平得到了很大的提高。
但是，对于城市化，我们不能只看到好的一面。由于人口增长太快，一些大城市出现了交通拥堵、住房紧张等问题。另外，很多年轻人进城工作，农村只留下了老人和孩子，这也是一个令人担心的社会问题。
总的来说，城市化既带来了机会，也带来了挑战。关于怎么解决这些问题，我们下节课继续讨论。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Good afternoon, everyone. Today let's talk about urbanization.
Over the past forty years, China has gone through the largest urbanization in the world: hundreds of millions of people moved from the countryside into cities. Urbanization made the economy grow fast and greatly raised the living standards of hundreds of millions.
But we can't see only the good side. Because the population grew too fast, some big cities developed problems like traffic congestion and housing shortages. Also, with young people leaving for city jobs, only the old and the young remain in the villages — a worrying social problem.
All in all, urbanization brings both opportunities and challenges. As for how to solve these problems — we'll continue next class.

readingQuestions.question: 过去四十年，中国经历了什么？
options: 世界上规模最大的城市化
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What has China gone through in the past forty years?

readingQuestions.question: 大城市出现了什么问题？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What problems appeared in big cities?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: 成语 are four-character set phrases — compressed stories that educated Chinese sprinkles everywhere. Start with six you can actually use.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Unpack the four characters (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 入乡随俗 enter-village-follow-customs = when in Rome. 半途而废 half-road-then-quit = give up halfway. Decode character by character and the phrase sticks.

helpMemoryTips.title: Placement matters
helpMemoryTips.text: Most 成语 slot in as predicates or adverbs: 他做事总是马马虎虎 (careless). Don't force them where a plain word belongs — sprinkled, not shoveled.

helpMemoryTips.title: Order inside the stack (Z19)
helpMemoryTips.text: Possessor → demonstrative+MW → clauses/phrases → adjectives → noun: 我昨天认识的那位年轻的中国记者. When it gets heavy, one 的 near the noun can carry several layers.

quizzes.title: Reading: 科技与生活
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: An HSK-5-style essay: balanced argument, formal frames (使, 对于, 由于, 关于, 则, 反而), and a quotable conclusion.

helpMemoryTips.title: 反而 = contrary to expectation
helpMemoryTips.text: 老人…反而被挡在门外 — instead (of being helped), they're shut out. 反而 flags an outcome that flips what the setup promised.

quizzes.readingPassage:
过去十年，科技使我们的生活发生了巨大的变化。移动支付让钱包成为历史；网上购物使人们足不出户就能买到世界各地的商品；人工智能则开始进入医院、学校和家庭。
对于这些变化，人们的态度并不相同。支持者认为，科技提高了效率，使更多人享受到了方便的服务。由于看病可以网上挂号，农村的病人再也不用半夜排队了。
但也有人担心：老人学不会用智能手机，反而被新技术挡在了门外；年轻人越来越依赖手机，面对面的交流却越来越少。
关于科技，也许最重要的问题不是"它能做什么"，而是"我们想让它为我们做什么"。技术本身没有好坏，使用它的方式才决定它的价值。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Over the past decade, technology has transformed our lives. Mobile payment made wallets history; online shopping lets people buy goods from all over the world without leaving home; and artificial intelligence is entering hospitals, schools and homes.
Attitudes toward these changes differ. Supporters argue technology raises efficiency and brings convenient services to more people. Since hospital registration works online now, rural patients no longer queue at midnight.
But others worry: elderly people who can't master smartphones end up shut out by the new technology, and the young grow ever more dependent on their phones while face-to-face conversation shrinks.
Perhaps the most important question about technology is not "what can it do" but "what do we want it to do for us". Technology itself is neither good nor bad — how we use it decides its value.

readingQuestions.question: 移动支付让什么成为历史？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did mobile payment make history?

readingQuestions.question: 有人担心谁被新技术挡在门外？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who do some worry is shut out by new technology?

readingQuestions.question: 文章认为，什么决定技术的价值？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: According to the essay, what decides technology's value?

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Reasoning tools: 既然…就 (since it's the case…), 否则 (otherwise), and the soft conditional tail …的话.

helpMemoryTips.title: 既然 ≠ 因为 (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 因为 gives a cause; 既然 leans on a fact both sides already accept: 既然你来了，就坐下吧 — since you're here anyway. It still wants its 就/也.

quizzes.title: Word-building: 化 / 性 / 主义

sentences.sentence: Urbanization changed the countryside. (city + 化) → ____改变了农村。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Three suffixes unlock hundreds of abstract words: 化 -ization (现代化), 性 -ness/-ity (重要性), 主义 -ism (乐观主义).

helpMemoryTips.title: Abstract Lego (Z7)
helpMemoryTips.text: 全球 globe + 化 = globalization; 可能 possible + 性 = possibility; 现实 reality + 主义 = realism. Spot the suffix, decode the stem — free vocabulary at C1 scale.

quizzes.title: Speaking: formal register delivery

subjects.display: 各位老师，各位同学，大家好。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Formal Mandarin is slower, evenly paced, fully toned — no swallowed syllables. Deliver these like a presenter.

helpMemoryTips.title: Formal = full syllables (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: Casual speech reduces; formal speech pronounces. Every 的, 了, 性 gets its full beat. Slow is not unnatural here — it's the register.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 造成 only breaks things

quizzes.title: Listening: 访谈 — 环境
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: An interview in educated, natural register — 越…越, 造成, 既然, and the rhetoric of advice.

helpMemoryTips.title: 从小事做起
helpMemoryTips.text: "Start from the small things" — 从 X 做起 is a set frame for advice; you'll meet it in every Chinese speech about change.

quizzes.readingPassage:
记者："李老师，您做环保工作二十年了。在您看来，最大的变化是什么？"
李老师："最大的变化是人们的态度。二十年前，很多人觉得环保跟自己没关系。现在，垃圾分类、少用塑料袋，已经成了很多家庭的习惯。"
记者："那么，最让您担心的问题是什么？"
李老师："是速度。经济发展得越快，对环境的压力就越大。如果我们只顾眼前的利益，就会给下一代造成无法挽回的损失。"
记者："对于普通人，您有什么建议？"
李老师："从小事做起。既然改变世界很难，那就先改变自己的生活方式。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Reporter: "Teacher Li, you've worked in environmental protection for twenty years. In your view, what's the biggest change?"
Li: "The biggest change is people's attitude. Twenty years ago, many felt the environment had nothing to do with them. Now sorting waste and cutting plastic bags are habits in many households."
Reporter: "And what worries you most?"
Li: "Speed. The faster the economy grows, the greater the pressure on the environment. If we only mind immediate gains, we'll cause the next generation irreversible losses."
Reporter: "Any advice for ordinary people?"
Li: "Start small. Since changing the world is hard, first change your own way of living."

readingQuestions.question: 李老师觉得最大的变化是什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Li see as the biggest change?

readingQuestions.question: 最让李老师担心的是什么？

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Homophones multiply at C1
helpMemoryTips.text: 事/是/市, 化/话/画 — the IME needs the whole word: type "chengshihua" (城市化) not syllable by syllable, and the right characters surface.

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇议论文
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A model argumentative essay: thesis, two supports, a concession, a turn — with 成语, 由于, 往往 and 反而 doing the heavy lifting.

helpMemoryTips.title: 欲速则不达
helpMemoryTips.text: "Desire speed, and you won't arrive" — a classical 成语 quoted mid-essay, exactly how educated prose deploys them (Z30).

quizzes.readingPassage:
在这个一切都追求"快"的时代，"慢"几乎成了一个贬义词。吃饭要快，走路要快，连休息都要"高效率"。然而，快真的总是好的吗？
首先，快容易使人马马虎虎。为了赶时间，我们常常把工作做得又快又糟，最后不得不花更多的时间去改正错误——欲速则不达，古人早就明白这个道理。
其次，快使我们失去了很多东西。由于急着赶路，我们看不见路边的风景；由于急着回消息，我们听不完朋友的一句话。生活的意义，往往就藏在这些被我们跳过的细节里。
当然，慢不等于懒。该快的时候快，该慢的时候慢，这才是真正的生活智慧。在人人都跑的时代，敢于慢下来，反而需要更大的勇气。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
In an era that chases "fast" in everything, "slow" has almost become a dirty word. Eat fast, walk fast — even rest must be "efficient". But is fast really always good?
First, speed breeds carelessness. Racing the clock, we do our work fast and badly, then spend more time fixing the mistakes — "haste brings no arrival," as the ancients already knew.
Second, speed costs us things. Rushing down the road, we miss the scenery beside it; rushing to answer messages, we don't hear a friend finish a sentence. Life's meaning often hides in exactly the details we skip.
Of course, slow is not lazy. Fast when it should be fast, slow when it should be slow — that is real wisdom about living. In an age when everyone runs, daring to slow down takes the greater courage.

readingQuestions.question: 文章说，快容易使人怎么样？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: According to the essay, what does speed breed?

readingQuestions.question: "欲速则不达"是什么意思？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does "yù sù zé bù dá" mean?

readingQuestions.question: 文章认为真正的生活智慧是什么？

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: News and reports swap everyday words for classical ones: 将 replaces 把 (and marks futures), 于 replaces 在 for time and place.

helpMemoryTips.title: Two 将s, one 于 (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 将 №1 = written 把: 请将手机关闭. 将 №2 = will: 会议将于九点举行. 于 = at/in/on after the verb or before the time: 生于1990年, 将于明日开幕.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't speak the written words
helpMemoryTips.text: 将/于/之 in casual conversation sounds like reading a news bulletin at dinner. Register runs both ways — these are for writing and formal speech only.

quizzes.title: 之 / 而 / 则

sentences.english: The south is rainy; the north, by contrast, is dry.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Three classical particles alive in modern prose: 之 = written 的, 而 joins with contrast or flow, 则 = "in that case / whereas".

helpMemoryTips.title: The classical trio (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 之 in set frames: 三分之一 (one third), 成功之路. 而 pivots: 简单而有效 simple yet effective. 则 balances clauses: 南方多雨，北方则干燥.

quizzes.title: Speaking: reading a news lead

subjects.display: 本次会议将于明日上午举行。
subjects.english: Běn cì huìyì jiāng yú míngrì shàngwǔ jǔxíng. — This meeting will be held tomorrow morning.

subjects.display: 据报道，该公司取得了创纪录的业绩。

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Read like a newsreader: measured pace, full tones, the written words given their full weight.

helpMemoryTips.title: News rhythm (Z30/Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: Broadcast Mandarin groups four-to-six syllables per breath-unit and never swallows finals. Match the voice's phrasing exactly.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Written Chinese has a passive palette: neutral 由 (handled by), receptive 受 (受到欢迎 well received), adverse 遭 (遭到破坏 suffered damage).

helpMemoryTips.title: Pick by flavour (Z23/Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 由 assigns responsibility, no drama: 会议由王教授主持. 受(到) receives, neutral-to-good: 受到好评. 遭(到) suffers, always bad: 遭到拒绝. 被 stays the everyday generalist.

quizzes.title: Listening: 新闻播报
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Two broadcast news items — 将于, 由…组成, 均, 之美: the written register read aloud, exactly as Chinese TV does nightly.

helpMemoryTips.title: 均 = written 都
helpMemoryTips.text: 所有活动均免费 — all events are free. 均 is 都 in a suit; you'll hear it only in announcements and read it everywhere (Z30).

quizzes.readingPassage:
晚上好，欢迎收看晚间新闻。
第一条：本市地铁五号线将于下月正式开通。新线路全长四十二公里，由二十八个车站组成。专家认为，五号线的开通将大大缓解市中心的交通压力。
第二条：本周末，第十二届国际图书节将在市图书馆举行。届时，来自三十多个国家的作家将与读者见面。本届图书节的主题为"阅读之美"。组织者表示，所有活动均免费向公众开放，详情可在图书馆网站查询。

Good evening, and welcome to the evening news.
Item one: the city's Metro Line 5 will officially open next month. The new line runs 42 kilometres and consists of 28 stations. Experts believe its opening will greatly ease traffic pressure downtown.
Item two: this weekend, the 12th International Book Festival will be held at the city library. Writers from more than thirty countries will meet readers. This year's theme is "The Beauty of Reading". The organizers say all events are open to the public free of charge; details on the library's website.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The written connective set: 然而 however, 因此 therefore, 此外 furthermore, 总之 in short — the skeleton of every essay and report.

helpMemoryTips.title: Match register across the sentence (Z25/Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 然而 belongs with 将/由/之; 可是 belongs with 把/在/的. Mixing (然而…啦!) jars like "however… gonna". Pick a register, keep it.

quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Questions that argue: 难道…吗? — "do you seriously mean…?"; 岂不(是) — "wouldn't that be…?". Both expect agreement, not answers.

helpMemoryTips.title: A question wearing armor
helpMemoryTips.text: 难道你忘了吗? — surely you haven't forgotten?! The literal question mark hides an exclamation. Use sparingly: one per argument hits hard, three per paragraph is melodrama.

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇社论
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A full editorial in 书面语: 然而/因此/此外/总之 as skeleton, 受到 passives, a rhetorical 岂不, and the closing 不在于…而在于.

helpMemoryTips.title: 不在于 A，而在于 B
helpMemoryTips.text: "lies not in A but in B" — the editorial's closing frame is a C1 essay staple. Steal it for your own conclusions (Z30).

quizzes.readingTitle: 社论：让城市为行人留一条路
quizzes.readingPassage:
近年来，本市机动车数量持续增长，人行道却越修越窄，部分路段甚至被停放的车辆完全占用。行人被迫走上机动车道，安全问题日益突出。
有人认为，城市的首要任务是保证交通效率，行人应当"让路"。然而，这种观点岂不是本末倒置？城市因人而生，为人而建。一座只方便汽车而不方便行人的城市，谈何宜居？
因此，我们呼吁：第一，有关部门应尽快清理被占用的人行道，违规停车行为必须受到处罚；第二，新建道路必须为行人和自行车留出足够的空间；此外，学校、医院周边路段应设置更多的过街设施。
总之，衡量一座城市的文明程度，不在于它的高楼有多高，而在于它对最普通的行人有多友好。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Editorial: Leave the pedestrians a path
In recent years, the number of motor vehicles in our city has kept growing while pavements are built ever narrower — some stretches are entirely occupied by parked cars. Pedestrians are forced onto the roadway, and safety problems grow by the day.
Some argue a city's first task is traffic efficiency, and pedestrians should "give way". But isn't that putting the cart before the horse? Cities exist because of people and are built for people. A city convenient for cars but not for walkers — how could it be called livable?
We therefore urge: first, the authorities should promptly clear the occupied pavements, and illegal parking must be punished; second, new roads must reserve adequate space for pedestrians and bicycles; furthermore, more crossings should be installed near schools and hospitals.
In short, a city's civilization is measured not by the height of its towers but by its friendliness to the ordinary person on foot.

helpMemoryTips.title: The wardrobe rule (Z30)

helpMemoryTips.title: Hear the suit change

quizzes.title: Big text: a report in 书面语
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A campus report with its register words removed. For each gap, pick the form that keeps the whole text in 书面语 — the casual twin is always lurking among the options.

helpMemoryTips.title: Register is a system (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: One 可是 in a report of 然而s breaks the suit. Choose by register first, grammar second — every option is grammatical, only one is dressed right.

quizzes.readingTitle: 关于图书馆使用情况的报告
quizzes.readingPassage:
关于图书馆使用情况的报告

本学期，图书馆的使用情况有了明显改善。与去年相比，每日到馆人数增长了三分之一。其中，周末的阅览室最受学生欢迎，常常座无虚席。
调查显示，大部分学生对新的开放时间表示满意，然而，也有部分同学建议，考试期间应将开放时间延长至晚上十一点。此外，自习区的座位仍然不足，高峰时段约有五分之一的学生找不到座位。
因此，我们建议：第一，增设两百个自习座位；第二，考试期间延长开放时间；第三，所有新措施均于下月起实行。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Report on library usage

This semester, library usage has clearly improved. Compared with last year, daily visits grew by one third. The weekend reading rooms are the most popular with students — often not an empty seat.
Surveys show most students are satisfied with the new opening hours; however, some suggest extending opening to 11 p.m. during exams. Furthermore, study-area seats remain insufficient: at peak times about one fifth of students cannot find a seat.
We therefore recommend: first, adding 200 study seats; second, longer hours during exams; third, all new measures to take effect from next month.

quizzes.title: Listening: 商务会谈
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Polite business Mandarin: 贵公司, 百忙之中, hedged objections with 恐怕, and a 由-passive in action.

helpMemoryTips.title: 贵 = your (honorable)
helpMemoryTips.text: 贵公司 your (esteemed) company, 贵姓? your honorable surname? — the politeness prefix that makes business Chinese purr.

quizzes.readingPassage:
"李总，欢迎欢迎！感谢您百忙之中抽时间与我们见面。"
"张经理客气了。贵公司的方案我们已经仔细研究过了。"
"您觉得怎么样？"
"总的来说，方案十分专业。不过，恐怕有两点需要再商量：第一，交货时间太紧，我们希望能延长两周；第二，关于售后服务的条款，写得不够具体。"
"您提的这两点都很有道理。这样吧，交货时间我们可以调整，售后条款今天下午就由法务部重新起草，明天发给贵公司。"
"好，那就这么定了。合作愉快！"
"合作愉快！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
"Director Li, welcome! Thank you for making time to meet us out of your busy schedule."
"You're too kind, Manager Zhang. We have studied your company's proposal carefully."
"What do you think?"
"Overall, it's very professional. But I'm afraid two points need more discussion: first, the delivery schedule is too tight — we'd like two more weeks; second, the after-sales clauses aren't specific enough."
"Both points are fair. How about this: we can adjust the delivery time, and our legal department will redraft the after-sales clauses this afternoon and send them to you tomorrow."
"Good, it's settled then. To a happy cooperation!"
"To a happy cooperation!"

helpMemoryTips.text: The written words have common homophones (将/讲, 于/与/雨). Register expectation — you KNOW a report says 将于 — beats the ear here (Z30).

quizzes.title: Reading: 两封信，两种语体
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: The same good news, twice: WeChat-casual and letter-formal. Read them side by side and collect the register pairs.

helpMemoryTips.title: Collect the pairs
helpMemoryTips.text: 拿到→收到录用通知, 那家→贵社, 就开始上班→将于…报到, 啦/吧/哈哈→此致敬礼. Same writer, ten minutes apart, two grammars (Z30).

helpMemoryTips.title: 哑巴英语
helpMemoryTips.text: "Mute English" — the (self-)mocking term for reading-only language skill. This course's speaking spine exists precisely so your Chinese won't be 哑巴中文.

quizzes.readingPassage:
甲："听说你最近在学英语？"
乙："对啊，学了三年了。"
甲："那你说两句让我听听。"
乙："这个……我的英语是哑巴英语——能听，能看，就是不能说。"
甲："那不就是收音机吗？"
乙："你别笑话我。你不是也学过法语吗？"
甲："我那法语学得可好了，法国人都夸我。"
乙："夸你什么？"
甲："夸我中文说得真棒！"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
A: "I hear you've been learning English lately?"
B: "Right, three years now."
A: "Say a couple of lines, let me hear."
B: "Well… mine is mute English — I can listen, I can read, I just can't speak."
A: "So… you're a radio?"
B: "Don't mock me. Didn't you study French too?"
A: "My French is superb — even the French praise me."
B: "Praise you for what?"
A: "For how brilliant my Chinese is!"

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇讽刺文章
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Satire runs on deadpan precision: mock-technical language (要领如下), ironic praise (令人叹为观止), and a twisted classic. Read for the sting under the smile.

helpMemoryTips.title: 与其说 A，不如说 B
helpMemoryTips.text: "Not so much A as B" — the essay's final turn. A precision instrument for reframing: 与其说是在看世界，不如说是在让世界看我们.

quizzes.readingPassage:
如今流行一种全新的旅游方式，我称之为"打卡式"旅游。其要领如下：到达景点后，第一时间找到最佳拍照角度，拍照三十张，修图十分钟，发朋友圈一条，然后——奔赴下一个景点。至于景点本身？看没看，重要吗？
这种旅游效率之高，令人叹为观止。有人一天"游"了八个景点，晚上数着朋友圈的点赞，满意地宣布：这个城市，我玩明白了。古人说"读万卷书，行万里路"；今人则是"拍万张照，修万张图"。
当然，我并非反对拍照。只是，当我们连一分钟都不肯留给风景本身，当点赞数成了旅行唯一的"成果"，我们与其说是在看世界，不如说是在让世界看我们——看我们忙着看手机。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
On "check-in" tourism
A brand-new style of travel is in fashion; I call it "check-in" tourism. The technique: on arriving at a sight, immediately locate the best photo angle, take thirty shots, retouch for ten minutes, post one WeChat update — then dash to the next sight. As for the sight itself? Seen or not — does it matter?
The efficiency is breathtaking. Some "tour" eight sights in a day, count their likes at night, and declare with satisfaction: this city — nailed it. The ancients said, "Read ten thousand books, travel ten thousand miles"; our contemporaries: "Take ten thousand photos, retouch ten thousand pictures."
I'm not against photography, of course. But when we won't spare the scenery even one minute, when likes become a journey's only "achievement" — we are not so much seeing the world as letting the world watch us… watching our phones.

readingQuestions.question: "打卡式"旅游最关心什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does "check-in" tourism care about most?

readingQuestions.question: "令人叹为观止"在文中是什么语气？
作者反对拍照吗？
options: 不反对，反对只拍照不看风景

helpMemoryTips.title: Say the setup, imply the point
helpMemoryTips.text: Natives often speak only the first half — 他现在是泥菩萨过江… — and let you finish it. Knowing the second half is the insider test (Z30).

quizzes.title: Listening: 文学朗读
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Literary prose read aloud — images, rhythm, and a closing antithesis. Listen once with eyes closed; comprehension questions after.

helpMemoryTips.title: 得到…却弄丢…
helpMemoryTips.text: The closing frame: gained X, yet lost Y. 却 is the literary "yet" — a hinge you'll hear in every reflective essay.

quizzes.readingTitle: 朗读：《家乡的秋》（散文节选）
quizzes.readingPassage:
在我的记忆里，家乡的秋天是有味道的。
是院子里桂花的甜香，混着新收的稻谷味儿；是母亲晒在竹竿上的辣椒，红得晃眼，辣得呛人。
那时候，日子过得慢。邮递员的自行车铃一响，半条街的人都探出头来；一封信，要读三遍：自己读一遍，念给奶奶听一遍，晚上躺在床上，在心里再读一遍。
如今我住在城里，秋天来了，只是手机上的一条消息："今日立秋。"我常想，我们得到了整个世界的消息，却弄丢了自己院子里的桂花香。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Reading: "Autumn in My Hometown" (prose excerpt)
In my memory, autumn in my hometown had a smell. It was the sweet scent of osmanthus in the courtyard mixed with newly harvested rice; it was the chilies my mother dried on bamboo poles — dazzling red, chokingly hot.
Days passed slowly then. When the postman's bicycle bell rang, half the street leaned out. A letter got read three times: once to yourself, once aloud to grandma, and once more at night, lying in bed, in your heart.
Now I live in the city, and autumn arrives as a phone notification: "Autumn begins today." I often think: we have gained the whole world's news, and lost the scent of osmanthus in our own courtyard.

readingQuestions.question: 在作者的记忆里，家乡的秋天有什么味道？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did hometown autumn smell of, in the author's memory?

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇书评
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A book review with a personality: ironic opener, concrete praise, an honest flaw, and 成语 (瑕不掩瑜, 大同小异) earning their keep.

helpMemoryTips.title: 瑕不掩瑜
helpMemoryTips.text: "The flaw doesn't hide the jade's luster" — THE set phrase for balanced reviews: acknowledge the defect, keep the praise (Z30).

quizzes.readingTitle: 书评：《深夜食堂里的中国》
quizzes.readingPassage:
这本书的书名起得极好，好到让人担心内容配不上它。读完之后可以放心了：担心是多余的——内容比书名还好。
作者花了五年时间，走访了三十个城市的夜宵摊。他写烤串，写馄饨，写凌晨三点的一碗热汤面，但归根结底，他写的是人：下了夜班的护士，刚吵完架的小两口，把一天的委屈就着啤酒咽下去的中年人。文字平实，却处处见功夫——没有一个字在炫技，也没有一个字是多余的。
当然，书也并非无可挑剔。后三分之一略显重复，几个城市的故事读起来大同小异。但瑕不掩瑜：在人人都写"大时代"的今天，有人愿意蹲下来，认认真真地写一碗面，这本身就值得敬佩。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Book review: "China at the Midnight Diner"
The title is so good you worry the book can't live up to it. Having finished it, you can relax: the worry was superfluous — the book is better than its title.
The author spent five years visiting late-night food stalls in thirty cities. He writes skewers, wontons, a bowl of hot noodle soup at 3 a.m. — but in the end he writes people: the nurse coming off a night shift, the young couple fresh from a quarrel, the middle-aged man washing the day's grievances down with beer. The prose is plain yet masterful everywhere — not one character shows off, and not one is wasted.
The book isn't beyond criticism, of course. The final third feels repetitive; several cities' stories read much the same. But the flaw doesn't obscure the jade: in an age when everyone writes "the great era", someone willing to crouch down and write one bowl of noodles with full seriousness deserves respect in itself.

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How long did the author spend visiting night stalls?

readingQuestions.question: 书评认为这本书归根结底写的是什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does the review say the book is ultimately about?

helpMemoryTips.text: "Our esteemed opponents" — the fixed courtesy address of Chinese debate. Attack the argument, honor the person (Z30).

quizzes.readingTitle: 辩论：人工智能会取代翻译吗？
quizzes.readingPassage:
主持人："今天的辩题是：人工智能会不会取代人类翻译？请正方发言。"
正方："谢谢主持人。机器翻译的进步有目共睹：速度快、成本低、错误率逐年下降。日常翻译的大部分工作，机器已经可以胜任。与其否认现实，不如承认：这个行业正在被重新定义。"
反方："对方辩友只看到了效率，却忽略了语言的本质。翻译不是简单的词语转换，而是文化之间的桥梁。机器可以翻译"再见"，但它翻译得出"长亭外，古道边"里的离愁吗？在文学、外交这些领域，人类翻译不但不会被取代，反而会因为机器的存在而变得更加珍贵。"
主持人："双方观点都很精彩。看来问题的关键，不在于机器能做什么，而在于我们把什么交给机器。"
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Debate: Will AI replace human translators?
Host: "Today's motion: will artificial intelligence replace human translators? The affirmative side, please."
Affirmative: "Thank you. Machine translation's progress is plain to see: fast, cheap, with error rates falling year by year. Machines can already handle most everyday translation. Rather than deny reality, better to admit it: this industry is being redefined."
Negative: "Our opponents see only efficiency and ignore the nature of language. Translation is not word-swapping but a bridge between cultures. A machine can translate 'goodbye' — but can it translate the parting sorrow in a classical verse? In literature and diplomacy, human translators will not be replaced; the machine's existence will make them more precious."
Host: "Both sides excellent. It seems the key is not what machines can do, but what we choose to hand them."

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇新闻分析
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: Journalistic analysis at full register: 表面上…实际上, 换言之, 综上所述, a porcelain metaphor, and a wordplay ending. Read for the argument's architecture.

helpMemoryTips.title: The pivot: 表面上…实际上
helpMemoryTips.text: "On the surface… in reality" — the analysis genre's signature move: open with the visible dispute, pivot to the structural one (Z30).

quizzes.readingTitle: 新闻分析：预制菜进校园之争
quizzes.readingPassage:
近日，多地家长对"预制菜进校园"表达担忧，相关话题连续数日占据热搜。表面上看，这是一场关于食品安全的争论；实际上，它触及的是一个更深层的问题：公共决策中的信任。
预制菜本身并非洪水猛兽。业内人士指出，规范生产的预制菜，其安全标准未必低于现场烹饪。然而，家长的愤怒并非毫无来由——真正令他们不安的，是"不知情"：孩子每天吃什么，竟需要通过网络爆料才能得知。
换言之，问题的核心不是"能不能吃"，而是"谁来决定、谁被告知"。有关部门若只强调检测合格，而回避决策程序的透明，恐怕难以真正平息质疑。信任如同瓷器，打碎容易，修复极难。
综上所述，与其在舆论发酵后被动回应，不如在决策之初就把家长请到桌前。毕竟，公共信任才是最经不起"预制"的东西。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
News analysis: the school pre-made meals controversy
Recently, parents in many cities voiced concern over "pre-made meals entering school canteens", and the topic dominated trending lists for days. On the surface it is a food-safety debate; in fact it touches something deeper: trust in public decision-making.
Pre-made meals are no monster in themselves. Industry insiders note that properly produced ones may meet safety standards no lower than on-site cooking. Yet the parents' anger is not groundless — what truly unsettles them is not knowing: they learned what their children eat daily only through online exposés.
In other words, the core issue is not "is it safe to eat" but "who decides, and who gets told". If the authorities stress only that tests were passed while avoiding transparency about the decision-making process, the doubts will hardly subside. Trust is like porcelain: easy to shatter, terribly hard to mend.
To sum up: rather than respond passively after public opinion boils over, better to invite the parents to the table when the decision is first made. Public trust, after all, is the one thing that cannot be "pre-made".

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Kill the imported scaffolding
helpMemoryTips.text: English needs pronouns, copulas and "when/if" glue everywhere; Chinese drops them. 当我吃饭的时候 → 吃饭时/吃着饭. "One of the most…" → …之一 used sparingly, or recast entirely.

helpMemoryTips.title: Topic first, verbs forward
helpMemoryTips.text: Natural Chinese fronts the topic and lets verbs run: not "我认为这是一个非常好的主意" every time — often just 这主意好. Shorter IS more native (Z28).

quizzes.title: Listening: 文化讲座
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A culture lecture that answers a question you've lived through this course: why hanzi survived. Full register: 非但…反而, 所谓, 乃在于.

helpMemoryTips.title: 非但…反而
helpMemoryTips.text: "Not only did it not…, on the contrary it…" — the strongest reversal frame in the language: 非但没有埋葬汉字，反而给了它新生.

quizzes.readingTitle: 讲座：汉字为什么没有消失
quizzes.readingPassage:
各位好。今天我们谈一个问题：汉字为什么没有消失？
一百年前，不少学者曾断言，汉字太难，必将被拼音文字取代。在打字机时代，这种担忧看似有理：西文打字机噼啪作响，汉字却连一台像样的打字机都造不出来。
然而，历史开了一个玩笑。计算机的出现，非但没有埋葬汉字，反而给了它新生：今天，输入汉字的速度丝毫不逊于任何拼音文字。所谓"汉字危机"，就这样烟消云散了。
更耐人寻味的是，正是最古老的特性救了汉字——它记录的是意义，而不仅仅是声音。正因如此，上海人和广州人口音天差地别，写下来却是同一行字；我们今天读两千年前的文章，居然还能会心一笑。
归根结底，汉字的生命力，乃在于它把整个文明装进了方寸之间。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Lecture: why did Chinese characters not disappear?
Greetings. Today's question: why didn't Chinese characters die out?
A century ago, many scholars declared characters too difficult — surely to be replaced by alphabetic writing. In the typewriter age the worry seemed reasonable: Western typewriters clattered away, while no decent Chinese typewriter could even be built.
History, however, played a joke. The computer, far from burying the characters, gave them new life: typing Chinese today is every bit as fast as typing any alphabet. The so-called "character crisis" vanished like smoke.
More thought-provoking still: it was the most ancient property that saved them — characters record meaning, not merely sound. That is why a Shanghainese and a Cantonese, whose accents differ like heaven and earth, write the very same line; and why we can read essays from two thousand years ago and still smile in recognition.
In the end, the vitality of the characters lies precisely in this: they pack an entire civilization into a square inch.

quizzes.title: Reading: 分析一篇短篇小说
quizzes.helpMemoryIntro: A complete flash story plus a critic's note — fiction and analysis in one sitting. Watch how the commentary reads meaning the story never states.

helpMemoryTips.title: 留白 — the unpainted space
helpMemoryTips.text: From ink painting: what's left blank carries the feeling. The critic's 不写一个"惨"字，而失落自现 is the C2 reading skill — hearing what the text declines to say.

quizzes.readingPassage:
【微型小说：修表匠】
老周修了四十年表。铺子小得转不开身，墙上却挂满了钟，每一只都走得分毫不差。
如今来修表的人少了。年轻人看时间用手机，"手表？那是装饰品。"
这天，一个姑娘拿来一只旧上海牌手表："我爷爷的。走不了了，师傅您看还有救吗？"
老周戴上放大镜，拆开表壳，看了很久。"零件早就不产了。"他说。姑娘的眼圈红了。
"不过，"老周从抽屉最里面摸出一个小铁盒，"我这儿还存着最后一套。"
表修好了。姑娘问多少钱，老周摆摆手："我只收修表的钱——零件不要钱。它等这只表，等了二十年了。"

【短评】
小说不足三百字，却写尽了一个时代。结尾一句是全篇之眼：等待的不是零件，而是老周自己——等一个还需要他的人。作者不写一个"惨"字，而失落自现；不写一个"暖"字，而温情自见。所谓留白，此之谓也。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
[Flash fiction: The Watch Mender]
Old Zhou has mended watches for forty years. His shop is too small to turn around in, yet the walls are covered with clocks, every one keeping perfect time.
Few come to mend watches now. The young check their phones: "A watch? That's jewellery."
One day a girl brings in an old Shanghai-brand watch: "My grandfather's. It's stopped — master, can it be saved?"
Old Zhou puts on his loupe, opens the case, looks a long while. "The parts went out of production years ago," he says. The girl's eyes redden.
"However —" Old Zhou reaches into the back of a drawer and brings out a small tin box, "I still keep one last set."
The watch is mended. The girl asks the price. Old Zhou waves a hand: "I charge only for the mending — the parts are free. They've been waiting for this watch for twenty years."

[Brief commentary]
In under three hundred characters, the story writes out an entire era. The final line is the eye of the piece: what waited was not the parts but Old Zhou himself — waiting for someone who still needed him. The author writes no word for "sad", yet the loss shows itself; no word for "warm", yet the tenderness appears. This is what is meant by leaving blank space.

helpMemoryTips.text: Once for the man, once for the craft: the numbers doing emotional work (两分钱, 三十六块), the refrain 可他还在游, and an ending that answers the question without answering it.

quizzes.readingPassage:
凌晨四点半，五十八岁的陈建国站在江边，把毛巾叠好，放进塑料袋。江水是黑的，只有对岸的灯，在水面上拉出几道细长的金线。
他游这条江，游了四十年。
一九八五年，他第一次横渡，是为了省两分钱的轮渡钱。那时他在对岸的纺织厂上班，一个月工资三十六块。"游过去，一个月能省下一块二，够给我娘买两斤猪肉。"
后来工厂倒了，轮渡停了，江上架起了三座大桥。地铁从江底穿过，八分钟一班。谁还需要游过去呢？
可他还在游。
"有人问我，桥都修好了，你游它干什么？"陈建国笑了，"我说，你们坐地铁，是为了到对岸去。我下水，不是为了对岸。"
医生说他的心脏比四十岁的人还好。老伴儿说他犟。儿子在深圳，视频里劝了十年："爸，危险。"他嘴上答应着，第二天四点半，闹钟一响，又拎起了塑料袋。
这些年，江水见过他结婚，见过他下岗，见过他送走母亲。水凉的时候，他知道秋天到了；水里漂着柳絮，他知道又是一年春天。"这条江认识我，"他说这话的时候，天边刚刚发白，"它比谁都清楚，我这一辈子，没偷过懒。"
五点整，他下水了。黑色的江面安静地裂开一道口子，又慢慢合上。对岸的灯一盏一盏地熄灭，城市醒了。
quizzes.readingPassageTranslation:
Feature: The Crosser
At half past four in the morning, 58-year-old Chen Jianguo stands at the river's edge, folds his towel and puts it in a plastic bag. The water is black; only the lights of the far bank pull thin gold threads across the surface.
He has swum this river for forty years.
His first crossing, in 1985, was to save the two-cent ferry fare. He worked then in the textile mill on the far side, at 36 yuan a month. "Swimming across saved one yuan twenty a month — enough to buy my mother two catties of pork."
Later the mill closed, the ferry stopped, three great bridges rose over the river. The metro runs beneath it, every eight minutes. Who still needs to swim across?
Yet he still swims.
"People ask me — the bridges are built, what do you swim for?" Chen laughs. "I tell them: you ride the metro to reach the far bank. I don't get in the water for the far bank."
The doctor says his heart is younger than a forty-year-old's. His wife says he's stubborn. His son in Shenzhen has spent ten years urging over video calls: "Dad, it's dangerous." He agrees out loud — and the next morning at 4:30, when the alarm rings, picks up the plastic bag again.
Over the years the river has seen him marry, seen him laid off, seen him bury his mother. When the water turns cold he knows autumn has come; when willow catkins drift on it, another spring. "This river knows me," he says, as the horizon just begins to pale. "It knows better than anyone that in this life of mine, I never once slacked."
At five sharp he enters the water. The black surface quietly splits open a seam, then slowly closes. On the far bank the lights go out one by one. The city wakes.

subjects.display: 如果有人问我，学中文最难的是什么，我不会说是声调，也不会说是汉字。
subjects.english: Rúguǒ yǒu rén wèn wǒ, xué Zhōngwén zuì nán de shì shénme… — If someone asks me what's hardest about learning Chinese…

subjects.display: 最难的，是敢于开口——从"你好"开始。
subjects.english: Zuì nán de, shì gǎnyú kāikǒu — cóng nǐ hǎo kāishǐ. — The hardest is daring to speak — starting from "nǐ hǎo".

subjects.display: 语言不是知识，而是一条要游过去的江。
subjects.english: Yǔyán bú shì zhīshi, ér shì yì tiáo yào yóu guòqù de jiāng. — A language is not knowledge but a river to be swum.

subjects.display: 桥再多，也代替不了自己下水。
subjects.english: Qiáo zài duō, yě dài tì bù liǎo zìjǐ xià shuǐ. — However many the bridges, they can't replace entering the water yourself.

subjects.display: 所谓精通，不过是每天都愿意再下一次水而已。
subjects.english: Suǒwèi jīngtōng, búguò shì měitiān dōu yuànyì zài xià yí cì shuǐ éryǐ. — So-called mastery is merely being willing to enter the water again, every day.
